• Ability to defend your design decisions, including putting the user need at the center of your case and align with overall business objectives

• Track record of shipping high quality web and/or mobile products and experiences

• Experience using web analytics software including Google Analytics and Heap

• Experience with multivariate (A/B) testing and agile iteration processes

• Ability to switch from high level strategic thinking to obsessing over pixel perfect UI

• Experience with Sketch, InVision, and Chrome Developer Tools

• Experience designing B2C products that help facilitate good decision-making and positive behavior change (preferred)

The secret to our sauce? Combining high technology with great design. Here are a few of the skills we value:

• Experience designing web or native apps. Your work shows a focused, user-centered approach to design.

• A talent for giving and receiving criticism, and an appreciation of its importance in the creative process.

• Experience in user research and user testing, and a data-informed (not data-driven) approach to design.

• Familiarity with Android’s Material Design and the iOS Human Interface Guidelines, and the role they play in native app design.

• Fluency in front-end code (HTML& CSS).

HOW TO APPLY

Does this sound interesting? If yes, please apply telling us about yourself. Include your résumé and a link to a succinct portfolio of your work. Let us know what you can contribute to the team. Include the title of the position you’re applying for and your name in the subject. Proofread! Make sure you spell and capitalize WordPress and Automattic correctly. We are lucky to receive hundreds of applications for every position, so try to make your application stand out. If you apply for multiple positions or send multiple emails there will be one reply.

Want to increase your chances of standing out? If so, please include the following in your email application:

What one single design (that you can share a link to) are you currently most proud of creating?

If you’re reading this on a site other than automattic.com please make sure you visit automattic.com/work-with-us for the latest details on applying and information about our fantastic benefits.

So, in summary: please e-mail us your letter with only one document attached (your résumé with your first and last name in the file’s title) and all other information provided as links (with any related info that we’ll need to access the content).

Curious who works in product at Automattic? Meet Kelly Hoffman and Mel Choyce !

About Automattic

Automattic wants to make the web a better place. Our family includes Jetpack, WooCommerce, Longreads, WordPress.com, and more. With WordPress.com, you can create beautiful websites and blogs for free and enhance those sites with our premium services. A fully distributed company, Automattic — celebrating ten years in 2015 — has over 500 staff in more than 50 countries.

Want to make the web a better place for more than a billion people each month? We’re hiring. Everyone works from the location they choose. We’re spread out all over the world in more than 50 countries. We track about 70 percent of our projects on P2-themed WordPress.com blogs, 25 percent in private chat rooms, and the rest on Slack. Because of the geographic variance, we’re active 24/7. We care about the work you produce, not just the hours you put in.

BENEFITS

• Open vacation policy (no set number of days per year). We encourage all employees to take the time they need for vacation, to pursue their own interests, to stay healthy, and to spend time with friends and family.
• Home office setup and coworking allowances. Working from a coffee shop? You can use your coworking allowance for the requisite latte!
• We happily provide or reimburse hardware and software you’ll need, as well as books or conferences that promote continued learning.
• Company-sponsored life insurance.
• Open maternity/paternity leave. If you’ve been with Automattic for 12 months, your leave is fully paid.
• WordPress-branded laptop at your four-year anniversary. A spiffy set of wireless headphones at your seven-year anniversary.
• Paid two to three-month sabbatical encouraged every five years.
• We cover all costs of company travel, so dust off that passport! Your team will get together one to three times per year in locations around the globe.
• Other benefits are country-specific, and include health, vision, and dental insurance; matching retirement/pension contributions; childcare vouchers; income protection; travel insurance; and discount offers.

Overview

Harvest is an independent software company making tools that help businesses run more smoothly. For the past 11 years, our customers have relied on our products as a critical part of their day-to-day operations. They’re the reason we’re still in business and our product decisions are driven by their needs.

The Harvest team started as a team of 3 and grew slowly to today’s current total of 51 lovely faces . Though we have an office in NYC, we hire the best people for the job no matter where they may call home. We’ve been working as a remote team since the beginning and we work hard to make sure everyone feels included and heard.

Product Design at Harvest

Whether we’re working to improve an older feature or adding something new, our product design team is responsible for the entire lifecycle of the process. We’re asked to lead customer research, determine areas of improvement or need for new features, design functional solutions, oversee implementation, and make sure our work tells a story. On any given day, we may find ourselves working with any team at Harvest—from customer support and marketing to engineering and ops.

Though keeping our team small has made for meaningful design work, lately we’ve found ourselves stretched thinner than we’d like to be. We feel that an experienced product designer will give us some breathing room and bring some new ideas to the table.

What We’re Looking For

These are the qualities we consider most important in a candidate:

• Much of our team collaboration happens in asynchronous, written mediums. Whether you’re sharing design rationale or giving constructive feedback, your words speak their meaning clearly and effectively.

• This isn’t an entry level job and your work isn’t theoretical. Your designs have seen real world use by actual humans.

• It’s not enough to bring good ideas to the table. Our designers rally support from their teammates and lead projects to completion.

• You’ve got a history of making design decisions that eschew trends, instead focusing on the people who will use your work.

• We all come to the table with different worldviews and experiences, but we can debate ideas because we share the goal of shipping the best possible solutions.

• We try to have fun together because, after all, it’s just a job.

You’ll notice we didn’t mention:

• We don’t care if you’re the kind of designer that mocks things up in a browser or prefers pixel perfect PSDs or Sketch files. The results are what matter.

• Likewise, we work the way that makes the most sense on a given project. We’re open to new approaches and so are you.

About Harvest

Harvest is a web-based time tracking and invoicing application relied on by over 40,000 creative businesses all across the globe. Harvest makes time tracking easy (and almost fun), keeping you on top of project budgets without the hassle of spreadsheets.

Harvest is one of the earliest Rails applications designed for businesses. We started as a team of 3, using Rails 0.14.1 (yes, we’re now on Rails 4.2). We remain a small and focused company, expanding our team only when absolutely necessary. Harvest is self-funded, profitable and has become an integral tool for tens of thousands of customers in over 150 countries. We write on Harvestʼs engineering blog.

We are a team of talented people working all over the globe. We genuinely care about our craft and demand the highest quality. Learn more about the human side of our company at the Harvest Watercooler. (Harvest Watercooler highlights the most human of modern activities: abandoning one of our blogs.)

Founded in 2012 in Amsterdam by the people behind Elasticsearch and Apache Lucene, Elastic set forth a vision that search can solve a plethora of data problems. The origins of the company start back in 2010 when Shay Banon wrote the first lines of Elasticsearch and open sourced it as a distributed search engine.

With the rise of cloud computing and changes in IT infrastructure demanding requirements such as real-time search across infinite amounts of structured and unstructured data, Shay foresaw the need for a new type of software to solve today’s real-world data problems. Steven Schuurman, Uri Boness, and Simon Willnauer shared in Shay’s vision, joining forces to create the Elastic company we have today.

Since then, the creators of Kibana, Logstash, and Beats have joined the Elastic family, rounding out a product portfolio known as the Elastic Stack, which is used by millions of developers around the world. The Elastic family unites employees across 32 countries into one coherent team, while the broader community spans across over 100 countries.

Instead of presenting static mocks, we build interactive HTML prototypes with AI and let stakeholders click through real flows, with real states and edge cases. Ideas get tested as working software early, which means we can explore several directions in the time it used to take to polish one.
AI is part of every phase of our process: research, ideation, UX writing, prototyping, and design system work. We also invest in our own tooling and reusable workflows so the whole team keeps getting faster. But AI doesn't make the decisions. What ships still comes down to a designer's judgment about the user, the business, and the product.

**About PhrasIQ**

PhrasIQ is decision infrastructure for enterprise finance. Growth-stage SaaS finance teams have abundant data but slow, low-confidence decision-making, caused by structural problems: spreadsheets, disconnected systems, manual processes, and unmanaged tooling. AI tools layered on unstructured data make this worse, not better, since there's no clear boundary between what's verified and what's inferred.

PhrasIQ fixes the root cause. Our architecture has two layers. Loktak is a deterministic backbone handling entity resolution, grounding scores, data lineage, and a versioned canonical finance ontology, targeting 99.8%+ accuracy on resolved matches, validated in internal testing. InsightOS is the orchestration layer on top, running forecasting, variance analysis, and narrative generation, and it reaches Loktak only through its API, never the database directly. That boundary means every output traces back to verified, lineage-tracked data.

CFOs and VPs of Finance can trust and act on forecasts in real time.

**About the Role**

We're building the design practice from zero. You'll own product design end to end: interaction design, visual systems, and the translation of a genuinely complex product (multi-agent orchestration, lineage-tracked data, forecasting workflows) into something a CFO can trust and actually use without a manual. You'll build the design system and process from scratch, not inherit one, and as the practice grows, you'll shape how design gets done here.

This is a founding role. Equity-only until seed close or $250K ARR, at which point cash compensation activates.

**What You'll Do**

* Own end-to-end product design for InsightOS's user-facing surfaces: forecasting workflows, narrative outputs, variance/anomaly review, agent interaction patterns
* Build design systems and process from zero, there isn't one yet
* Translate deterministic/probabilistic architecture into interfaces that build user trust rather than confusion (e.g., surfacing what's verified vs. inferred)
* Work directly with the founder and engineering team on product decisions, not just visual execution
* Set the design standards and workflows that shape how the team designs going forward

**What We're Looking For (Core Qualities)**

* Builder Mindset: you'd rather ship something imperfect than plan something perfect
* Design/Product Taste: you have a point of view on what makes an interface trustworthy, not just polished
* Systems Thinking: you can hold a complex, multi-layer product in your head and design for its actual architecture, not just its screens
* Ownership: you don't wait to be told what to design next
* Speed & Efficiency: you move fast without needing everything spelled out
* Learning Velocity: you can get fluent in enterprise finance workflows quickly
* Communication: you can defend design decisions to engineers and founders, not just present them
* Mission Alignment: you care about the deterministic-first, auditable-first thesis, not just about making things look good

**Compensation**

Equity-only until seed close or $250K ARR. This is a founding-level equity stake, not an intern or contractor arrangement.

**Filter Questions (Screening)**

* This is equity-only with no cash until seed close or $250K ARR. What makes that worth it for you right now?
* You'd be building our design system and process from scratch. Walk us through how you'd spend your first two weeks.

## About MyArchitectAI

MyArchitectAI is an AI rendering platform used by architects, interior designers, and visualization professionals in over 150 countries. We turn CAD designs, sketches, and line drawings into photorealistic renders in seconds, with no installs, no hardware requirements, and no learning curve.

We're a team of 5, fully remote, spread across Europe.

## Why we're hiring

Our product works. Our retention and engagement has a lot of room for improvement. Too many people sign up, render a few images, and never come back, or cancel when their current project ends. We have the data (PostHog, Stripe, cancel surveys, live chat) and we have the engineers. What we don't have is one person whose job is to find the leaks and fix them.

That's you.

## What you'll own

**Activation and engagement**
Dig into user behavior in PostHog and Supabase. Figure out where people get stuck between signup and their first "wow" render, and why paying users stop rendering. Turn that into a prioritized list of experiments, run them, and report what moved.

**UX improvements**
Take existing flows and make them simpler and nicer to look at. Our users judge us on how good the app looks, because that's their job. You'll design in Claude Design on top of our existing design system (and improve it), so you do need taste and the ability to tell good from almost good.

**New features from scratch**
From problem to shipped. Talk to users, define the feature, design it, write a spec, QA it on staging, ship it, measure it.

## Who this is for

- You've been a PM, growth PM, or product designer at a SaaS company, ideally one selling to non-technical users. B2B or prosumer both fine.
- You're comfortable doing your own analysis. Funnels, cohorts, SQL, experiment design, knowing when a result is noise.
- You have visual taste and opinions about UI. You can look at a screen and clearly explain why it feels off.
- You write clearly. Most of your output will be specs, hypotheses, and short reports, and other people have to act on them.
- You're self-directed. Nobody will assign you tickets. You'll find the problems yourself.

## Who this is not for

- People who need a designer, an analyst, and an engineer to get anything done.
- People who want to write strategy docs or call all-hands. We need someone who ships fast.

## The deal

- Around 20 hours a week to start. Can grow to full-time if it works for both sides.
- We start with a paid, scoped project so we both see how it goes. If it's good, we move to a monthly retainer.
- You invoice us as a contractor. Location doesn't matter.

## How we work

- Fully remote and mostly async.
- Specs go into Linear. Design happens in Claude Design. Analysis happens in PostHog and SQL.
- We use AI tools heavily and expect you to as well. If you're skeptical of AI-assisted design and coding, this isn't the right place.
- Short feedback loops. You'll get a yes or no within hours, not a week.
- You'll talk to real users. Support is handled by the founders, and you'll have access to every conversation.

## How to apply

Skip the cover letter. Send us:

1. One thing you shipped that moved a metric, and what it moved.
2. Why you're a good fit.
3. Your rate assuming 20hrs/week.

Keep it short. We read everything.

The garden3d Head of Design has one mandate: nothing we put on the internet falls below an 8 out of 10. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and all of them ship work into the world under our name. Working in close partnership with our founder & president [Hugh Francis](http://hhff.solar/), this person sets the craft standard, and builds the culture that holds it.

**You can be based anywhere**. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.

This role works with studio leads, designers, developers, editors, animators, photographers and clients across every garden3d vertical.

This person can move between a brand identity, a product interface, a case study and a launch film in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.

They span all of garden3d, but their home base is [XXIX](https://www.xxix.co/). Our design studio is where the standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips, so this person runs critique there. Regular reviews. Honest and specific feedback. A shared language for why one thing is better than another, and what practically to do about it. They are also how we get better people. ### 🧲 **Hiring and empowering the very best**

They are a magnet for exceptional designers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so.

They run new business for design. Pitching, scoping and closing the work we actually want, and building the relationships that bring the next one back. When a project is our highest-profile or highest-budget, they're in it: not always as the day-to-day lead, but as the person shaping the creative direction and making sure it lands. The work we win, and the work we're known for, is the clearest measure of whether this is going well.

### ✍️ **Type and editorial design**

Typography and editorial systems are core craft here, not a specialism we farm out. This person has a real practice in both. Their type choices should be one of the first things you notice about their portfolio, and one of the first things our designers learn from them.

### 📚 **Case study production**

Every engagement across our studios should end in a case study you'd want to read. Producing them is second nature to this person: interviewing the team, shaping the narrative, art-directing the assets, and shipping something that wins the studio its next project.

### 🖥️ **Websites that put our best foot forward**

Our sites are usually the first place a prospective client or hire meets us. This person owns what each garden3d site says, what work it shows, and how clearly it explains what that studio can do. They keep sites, decks and collateral current as the work moves, so what people find is sharp and true.

### 🎪 **Presence IRL**

garden3d shows up in person: events, conferences, talks, Index programming, and the dinners and openings where our world gathers. This person decides which of these deserve our time, gets us there looking like ourselves, and comes back with something to publish.

### 🌭 **Culture**

They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The designers they lead do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is earned, and the taste rubs off.

### 🔥 Special Projects
In addition to day to day responsibilities, here’s an idea of some of the projects this role may spearhead or support in coming years →
- Building XXIX's critique practice into something other studios try to copy
- Landing the kind of flagship design engagement that changes what people think we do
- Hiring the next generation of the design team, across every garden3d studio
- Rebuilding our studio websites so each one sells its studio properly
- A case study production line that feeds all four new-business pipelines
- Bringing our type and editorial practice into garden3d TK: books, covers, records, screenplays

**ABOUT LENOX PARK SOLUTIONS**

Lenox Park Solutions’ mission is to use collaborative technology and data science to democratize opportunity access, primarily in the financial services industry.
Lenox Park Solutions is an early-stage FinTech company developing innovative tools and resources to enhance collaboration and data-driven decision-making for investors and financial professionals. With a strong foundation in investment banking and asset management, the company has honed technological best practices through partnerships with some of the world’s most respected investment firms.
At the core of Lenox Park Solutions’ offerings is ‘RoundTables’, an exclusive, cloud-based data platform, which enables organizations to efficiently and securely gather and centralize relevant metrics and data. This allows decision makers to measure ‘Impact’ to inform and assess investment decisions. Lenox Park Solutions has successfully introduced its technology to the marketplace, attracting a prestigious client base that includes some of the most sophisticated and globally well-respected investment institutions.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

We are seeking a fractional UX/UI DESIGN PARTNER (an independent designer or a small design firm) to bring dedicated design attention to RoundTables, Lenox Park Solutions’ platform. The engagement reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and works in close, hands-on collaboration with the engineering team, the Product Manager, and the client services team; the colleagues on the front lines with the platform’s day-to-day users and with the clients who rely on RoundTables for reporting and survey administration. This is the company’s first dedicated design role: to date, design has been handled in-house only informally, by team members whose primary responsibilities lay elsewhere, and bringing in focused design expertise is a deliberate next step for a maturing platform.
Lenox Park Solutions has invested substantially in RoundTables including professional design work delivered through a previous external design engagement and the platform already serves a sophisticated client base. This is not a rebuild or a redesign from scratch; it is an opportunity to take strong, established work and make it better for the people who use it. The focus is on enhancing the experience of current users: bringing greater consistency to the design, refining the most important workflows, and closing the gap between design intent and what reaches production. A core part of the engagement is developing a deep understanding of the user journey which may include research with Lenox Park’s clients and the asset owners, asset managers, and survey administrators who use RoundTables ensuring design decisions are grounded in real use.

**RESPONSIBILITIES & QUALIFICATIONS**

As Lenox Park Solutions’ UX/UI Design Partner you will:

1. Work with the platform as it exists today and make it clearer, more consistent, and easier to use.
2. Develop a deep understanding of the RoundTables user journey including, where useful, research with clients and end users, and apply it to refine the platform’s most important experiences, such as the dashboards and workflows used by survey hosts, survey takers, and administrators, the survey-taking experience, the manager impact report, and contact-list management.
3. Bring consistency to the platform’s existing design language, establishing clear, brand-aligned standards and reusable patterns in Figma so design and engineering stay aligned and new work ships faithfully.
4. Collaborate closely and iteratively with the engineering team, the Product Manager, and the client services team, producing development-ready specifications and handoff documentation so that what reaches production matches what was designed.

The ideal designer or firm brings:

1. Demonstrated experience designing and shipping B2B SaaS or data-platform interfaces, ideally complex, data-dense web applications, supported by a portfolio of end-to-end UX and UI work.
2. A strong UX foundation in user research, role-based information architecture, and user-journey mapping, with the ability to translate how a product is actually used into clear, prioritized design improvements.
3. Proven skill in working within an existing product, refining and enhancing live interfaces and bringing consistency to an established design language, rather than rebuilding from the ground up.
4. Fluency with Figma for design standards, reusable components, and accessible, WCAG-aligned patterns, alongside a rigorous, developer-ready handoff practice that keeps production output faithful to the agreed design.
5. A self-directed, collaborative operating style suited to a fractional, milestone-based independent engagement, and comfort working hands-on alongside an internal engineering, product, and client services team.

**COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS**

This is a fractional, independent-contractor engagement rather than a salaried employee position, and compensation is milestone-based rather than hourly. Each phase of work, from user-journey research through refined platform workflows, design standards, and developer handoff, is tied to a defined deliverable and a fixed fee agreed in advance, so investment is predictable and linked directly to completed outcomes.
• Independent-contractor (1099) engagement; open to either an individual designer or a design firm.
• Compensation structured as fixed fees tied to agreed project milestones and deliverables, rather than hourly billing.
• Milestones, deliverables, and fees defined and scheduled with the selected designer or firm before work begins, with payment on acceptance of each completed milestone.
• A fractional, project-scoped engagement, with the possibility of an ongoing design retainer once the initial milestones are complete.

**BENEFITS**

As an independent-contractor engagement, this role is not eligible for the employee benefits programs offered to Lenox Park Solutions’ US-based staff which include medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, health and wellness reimbursement, and a 401(k) plan.

**LOCATION**

Remote. Lenox Park Solutions’ staff work remotely, as we believe team members are most productive when they live in the places they choose and establish schedules that offer flexibility. Certain meetings may take place in person and require physical presence in New York City.

**COME WORK WITH US!**

If this opportunity sounds appealing to you, please email a resume and a portfolio — or, for firms, representative case studies — to lps.careers1@lenoxparkinc.com. A brief note describing relevant SaaS or data-platform design work and your approach to design systems is encouraged but optional.

**DEADLINE TO APPLY: **Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

**OPTIMIZING HUMAN CAPITAL**

At Lenox Park, we measure diversity rather than describe it. We built the Lenox Park Impact Score (LPI), in collaboration with our clients, to benchmark human capital optimization across ownership, leadership, and workforce on both gender and racial/ethnic dimensions, and we hold our own firm to the standard we set for everyone else. **Company:** GreenChoice, PBC, the food intelligence company
**Employment Type:** Full-Time
**Location:** India (preferred) or Remote
**Experience:** 3 to 5 years

**We have multiple roles open—Please apply to only one role where you see a strong fit with your skills and experience.**

### About GreenChoice
GreenChoice, PBC is the leading public benefit food health intelligence company. GreenChoice gives 40+ food retail and technology partners instant access to personalized nutritional guidance, evidence-based food health scores, and verified health attribute data on over 1 million food products, with award-winning integrations to meet consumers' changing health needs and provide medically tailored food-as-medicine benefits. GreenChoice has already guided over 10 million healthier purchases. Google named GreenChoice one of the three "Best Apps for Good" in the U.S.

GreenChoice is backed by Katapult and BonBillo Ventures, partners with Stanford University School of Medicine, and members of the Tufts Friedman School Food & Nutrition Innovation Council. GreenChoice is guided by a Science Advisory Board of leading PhDs, dietitians, and researchers in public health, nutrition science, environmental science, and behavior change.

### About the Role
As a Front End Engineer at GreenChoice, you will both design and build the web and mobile experiences our users interact with every day. This is a dual role. You will create the designs yourself, in Figma, and then bring them to life in React.js and React Native with Expo. You own the experience end to end, from the first wireframe to the shipped, responsive interface.

We are not looking for someone who only implements other people's mockups. You will be the person deciding how a feature should look and behave: mapping the user flow, designing the screens, prototyping the interactions, and then writing the code that makes it real. That means strong design judgment matters as much as strong engineering skills here.

You will work closely with product and backend engineers to ship features that feel fast, look right, and are genuinely easy to use. This role suits someone who is equally comfortable in a design file and a code editor, cares deeply about the details of the user experience, and wants full ownership of front end features from concept through production.

### Key Responsibilities
**Design:**
* Own the UI/UX for front end features: take a problem or product idea and design the flow, screens, and interactions for it.
* Create wireframes, mockups, and interactive prototypes in Figma, and iterate on them based on feedback.
* Make the call on layout, visual hierarchy, typography, color, spacing, and interaction patterns so the result is clear and easy to use.
* Define and maintain a consistent visual and interaction language across web and mobile.
* Design the full picture, including the states that are easy to forget: loading, empty, error, edge cases, and responsive breakpoints.

**Frontend Development:**
* Build and maintain web applications with React.js and mobile applications with React Native and Expo.
* Implement your own designs as high-quality, pixel-accurate interfaces.
* Implement responsive design and ensure cross-browser and cross-platform compatibility.
* Manage application state cleanly using Redux, Context API, or similar tools.
* Build reusable, well-structured components and front end patterns.

**Integration and Collaboration:**
* Work with backend engineers to integrate REST and GraphQL APIs and ensure smooth data flow into the UI.
* Participate in code reviews and front end technical discussions.

**Quality and Maintenance:**
* Write unit and component tests to keep the interface stable.
* Keep code clean, well-documented, and reusable.
* Debug, optimize, and monitor front end performance, including load times and rendering.

**Required Skills and Qualifications**
* 3 to 5 years of experience, with a track record of both designing and building front end interfaces.
* Strong design ability: you can create your own designs in Figma (wireframes, mockups, prototypes), not just implement someone else's.
* A real grasp of UI/UX fundamentals: usability, visual hierarchy, typography, color, spacing, and interaction patterns.
* A portfolio or examples of work that show both the design and the built result.
* Strong proficiency in:
1. React.js
2. React Native with Expo
3. JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3
* Experience with state management tools (Redux, Context API).
* Solid understanding of responsive design, cross-browser compatibility, and accessibility.
* Proficiency with Git and collaborative tools (Asana, Slack, code versioning workflows).
* Comfortable consuming and integrating REST and GraphQL APIs.
* Able to work independently in a startup environment and own features end to end, from design to deployment.

**Nice to Have**
* Experience with TypeScript.
* Familiarity with front end testing frameworks (Jest, Cypress, React Testing Library).
* Experience optimizing performance for mobile and low-bandwidth conditions.
* Experience building or maintaining a design system or component library.
* Familiarity with user research, usability testing, or analytics to inform design choices.
* A formal background or training in design (visual, interaction, or product design).
* An interest in sustainability, food systems, or health tech.

### What We Offer
* Salary: $15000-$20000 USD per year (based on location & experience).
* Equity options in a growing early-stage startup.
* Flexible working hours and remote work opportunities.
* Mission-driven team with a collaborative and inclusive culture.
* A chance to have a real-world impact on how people eat and live healthier, more sustainable lives.

About the Role

We're seeking freelance UX/UI Designers who specialize in design systems to help our clients modernize their systems for a world where humans and AI tools build side by side. Some companies call this a Design Engineer or Systems Designer; we're using UX/UI Designer, Design Systems here because it's the clearer, more searchable term for what this role actually is: a design role, not a software engineering one. This role sits at the intersection of design systems craft and AI fluency: someone who's equally comfortable untangling a token architecture in Figma and configuring the AI-tooling connections (MCP and similar) that let coding assistants read and respect that system instead of guessing at it. Contract projects typically range from ten to forty hours per week, depending on client needs and project scope, and often run as focused, timeboxed engagements rather than open-ended retainers.

Responsibilities

•
Audit existing design systems for structural gaps: tokens versus variables, component architecture, and missing or outdated documentation.

•
Resolve foundational issues (naming, token structure, variable setup) so a design system translates cleanly into documentation and code, without introducing breaking changes for engineering.

•
Build and maintain design system documentation, covering components, patterns, usage guidelines, and variant rules, in a structured format built for AI-fluent workflows and legible to both humans and AI tools.

•
Configure and maintain AI-tooling connections between design platforms (Figma, documentation platforms) and AI coding or design assistants (Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, Figma Make, GitHub Copilot, and similar), often via MCP-style integrations.

•
Extract undocumented institutional knowledge from designers and engineers and turn it into clear, actionable documentation.

•
Establish or refine governance models, contribution workflows, and success metrics so a design system stays healthy after the engagement ends.

•
Collaborate closely with design and engineering stakeholders, translating between the two without needing to write production code.

•
Stay current on evolving AI-assisted design and design-to-code workflows as the tooling landscape shifts.

Requirements

•
Strong experience in design systems, UX/UI design, or design engineering, with real depth at the foundational level (tokens, variables, component architecture), not just visual component work.

•
Genuine, hands-on fluency with AI-assisted design or coding tools, and enough technical comfort to configure AI-tooling connections rather than just use them.

•
Strong written communication skills. A lot of this work is turning tribal knowledge into documentation other people (and AI tools) can actually rely on.

•
Comfortable working independently on defined, timeboxed engagements with light day-to-day oversight.

•
Adaptable to different company environments, including regulated or compliance-sensitive ones where design-to-production handoffs stay manual by design.

Tools & Platforms

•
Figma, including Dev Mode, variables, and component architecture.

•
Design system documentation platforms: zeroheight preferred, with Supernova, Backlight, Frontify, or similar also valued.

•
AI-assisted design and coding tools: Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, Figma Make, GitHub Copilot, and other MCP-compatible platforms.

•
Familiarity with how design tokens map into code (CSS variables, JSON tokens, Style Dictionary-style pipelines) is a plus.

Summary Generated by Built In

Who We Are
Neighborly Software was built to help communities make a difference in the lives of low-income families and vulnerable populations. Our mission is simple, “Helping Communities, Help People.”

Headquartered in Atlanta, GA we offer a cloud-based technology platform for the administration and disbursement of governments funds for programs such as Housing, Economic, Community Development, Disaster Recovery/MIT, Home Energy Rebate Programs, and Housing Choice Voucher programs.

Role Overview

The UX Lead is the first dedicated user experience role at Neighborly Software. Our users — government agency staff, nonprofit administrators, contractors, and the residents and applicants they serve — rely on the platform to run complex, high-stakes programs where clarity matters. The UX Lead owns how that platform looks, feels, and flows.

This is a founding, individual-contributor role with no direct reports. You will build the design practice from the ground up — a design system and reusable component library, documented personas and user journeys, a standard style guide, and accessibility and responsive design as standing norms — while remaining hands-on with the design work itself. Because the role carries no team, it leads through influence: setting a direction that product managers, engineers, and QA choose to follow because the thinking is sound and the work makes theirs better.

Beyond producing design artifacts, you will set standards and hold the organization to them, guiding product, engineering, and QA toward a simpler, lower-friction experience. Success is measured in friction removed: fewer clicks, clearer workflows, visible status and feedback, and interfaces that embrace a “don’t make me think” philosophy. This is an opportunity to take the platform into its next phase and align the experience with where the company is headed.

Core Attributes:

•
Owner — treats the platform experience as their responsibility end to end, and holds the standard when it would be easier to let it slide.

•
Systems thinker — sees the reusable pattern behind the one-off request and builds for reuse.

•
Simplifier — instinctively removes steps, clicks, and cognitive load.

•
Voice of the customer — advocates for the user in rooms where the user is not present, grounded in research rather than opinion.

•
Leads without a team — earns influence through credibility, clarity, and collaboration rather than reporting lines.

•
Pragmatic builder — ships improvements incrementally rather than waiting on a perfect, all-at-once redesign.

Key Responsibilities:

Design System and Standards

•
Build and own a design system — a reusable component library, interaction patterns, and usage guidance that product, engineering, and QA work from.

•
Establish and maintain a style guide for consistent branding across the platform, aligned with company positioning and messaging.

•
Establish accessibility as an organizational norm — set WCAG-based standards, build accessible patterns into the design system, and define how compliance is validated before release.

•
Establish responsive design as an organizational norm so the platform behaves predictably across desktop, tablet, and mobile.

•
Hold the organization accountable to these standards, reviewing work in progress and partnering with product and engineering leadership when the bar isn’t met.

Experience Design and Simplification

•
Redesign core workflows to reduce friction — fewer clicks, clearer paths, and meaningful status and feedback.

•
Modernize and simplify the interface, both visually and in how users interact with it.

•
Guide user experience solutioning for known pain points, turning recurring customer complaints into designed, validated solutions.

•
Assess core functionality for reuse across personas and program types — for example, extending an existing capability into a contractor portal — without fragmenting the product.

Research, Personas, and Voice of the Customer

•
Build and document personas and user journeys, and keep them current as a shared reference for product, engineering, marketing, and sales.

•
Join client calls and discovery sessions with product managers to gather firsthand feedback and translate it into design direction.

•
Lead workshops — discovery sessions, journey mapping, design reviews, and prioritization exercises — with internal teams and customers.

Prototyping and Cross-Functional Partnership

•
Establish prototyping norms and a shared framework with the product team so concepts are tested visually before reaching engineering.

•
Guide engineering and QA on implementation fidelity, component reuse, and front-end quality, so what ships matches what was designed.

•
Partner with engineering on front-end performance and observability (for example New Relic), treating perceived speed as a design concern.

Measurement

•
Use product analytics (for example Pendo) to understand user behavior, identify friction points, and validate whether design changes improved outcomes.

•
Define and track experience metrics — task completion, time on task, error rates, support volume — and report progress to leadership.

•
Performs other duties as required.

First-Year Outcomes:

•
A documented design system and component library in active use by product and engineering.

•
A published style guide, with consistent branding applied across the platform’s primary modules.

•
Accessibility and responsive design standards defined and built into the design and QA process.

•
Documented personas and user journeys adopted as shared reference across product, engineering, marketing, and sales.

•
A working prototyping practice established with the product management team.

•
Measurable friction reduction in at least two high-traffic workflows, evidenced by analytics.

Required Qualifications:

•
Bachelor’s degree in Design, Human-Computer Interaction, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

•
5+ years of user experience and user interface design experience, including time as the lead or senior-most designer on a product or platform.

•
A portfolio demonstrating end-to-end ownership of complex, workflow-heavy applications — not solely marketing sites or consumer apps.

•
Demonstrated experience building a design system and component library from the ground up and driving its adoption.

•
Hands-on expertise with modern design and prototyping tools (for example Figma), including component libraries, design tokens, and interactive prototypes.

•
Working knowledge of accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA or later) and experience designing and validating accessible interfaces.

•
Demonstrated experience delivering responsive design across desktop, tablet, and mobile.

•
Direct experience conducting user research and synthesizing findings into personas, journeys, and design decisions.

•
Experience facilitating workshops and design reviews with cross-functional and customer audiences.

•
Demonstrated ability to lead as an individual contributor — influencing engineering, QA, and product partners, and holding a standard across teams that don’t report to you.

•
Experience with product analytics tools and using behavioral data to inform design decisions.

Working fluency with AI tools applied to design and research — synthesis, content drafting, and rapid concept generation.

Excellent communication and presentation skills, including explaining design rationale to executives, engineers, and customers.

Enough familiarity with HTML, CSS, and component-based front-end frameworks to have productive technical conversations with engineers.

The Role

Lead the product's presentation layer: visual design, motion/interaction, and design system ownership in Figma. Produce implementation-ready motion specs (Lottie/AE/Bodymovin), create identity-driven, action-oriented cross-platform experiences for iOS/Android/Web, collaborate with engineers, and ship quickly in a startup using AI-assisted tools.

Summary Generated by Built In

We are seeking a Senior UX Interface Designer with a genuine, discerning visual sensibility who can recognize the difference between a screen that merely functions and one that commands attention, builds trust, and makes an athlete want to keep coming back. This is not a role for someone who executes a design system without aesthetic judgment. We need a designer who has a point of view, can defend it, and can elevate our product visually while remaining disciplined within our design constraints.

This role owns the Presentation Layer — how the product is formatted in terms of fonts, graphics, and animation, along with intuitive navigation. Key focus areas include innate visual design sensibility applied to a premium dark-surface consumer product; identity-driven, personalized experiences that adapt to each user's performance profile; high-quality motion and interaction design that communicates performance and progress; and action-oriented workflows that eliminate passive data consumption.

This is a startup environment where the ideal candidate thrives building from 0->1, is comfortable with ambiguity, and takes ownership rather than waiting for direction. We move fast, hold a high visual standard, and ship against hard dates. We also leverage modern AI-assisted development tools to accelerate delivery; comfort in these environments is a must.

Key Tasks & Responsibilities

Visual Design Leadership (Defining Responsibility)

• Own the overall aesthetic standard of the product: typography application, spatial rhythm, depth hierarchy, color restraint, icon quality, and component polish

• Ensure the product reads as a premium consumer tool — not a clinical health app, generic fitness tracker, or scaled-up spreadsheet

• Apply visual judgment to commercial surfaces (marketplace, subscription tiers, upsell moments) while maintaining trust in the system

• Build and maintain the authoritative Figma (or equivalent) design system: token library (colors, type ramps, spacing, radius, motion), component library, and identity cell documentation

Identity-Driven & Personalized Experience Design

• Design the identity recoloring moment in onboarding as the signature emotional beat of the product — a real-time ambient palette transition that feels intentional, earned, and beautiful

• Ensure the primary dashboard identity symbols function coherently as both the user's visual identity expression and the entry point to the AI coaching layer

• Design the shareable identity card in both quiet (clean, restrained) and expressive (gamified, bold numbers) aesthetic modes

• Ensure scoring loops, streak mechanics, and progression tier displays feel motivating and identity-consistent — not a generic gamification model

Motion Design & Interaction (Critical)

• Design and spec all animated moments, including the readiness score arc animation, the pre-launch cinematic welcome experience, identity ambient recolor, mission/achievement completion states, AI coaching insight reveals, and score/pillar change reveals

• Define motion standards for the full product: screen transitions, micro-interactions, press states, loading states, skeleton screens, empty states, and error states

• Produce implementation-ready motion specs for multiple devices: Bodymovin/Lottie files, timing curves, duration values, and engineering handoff notes

UX/UI Design Across the Full Screen Inventory

• Design action-oriented experiences that tell the user what to do next; every screen should have a clear direction rather than a passive display of data

• Translate complex biomarker, wearable, and AI-generated data into interfaces that are immediately readable and emotionally resonant — not dense, clinical, or overwhelming

• Design the dashboard priority engine as the product's daily engagement surface — one that feels like a coach, not a notification list

• Design an AI coaching modal as a distinct experience layer, and maintain high-fidelity designs across iOS, Android, and Web simultaneously (design once, build anywhere)

Cross-Platform Consistency & Engineering Collaboration

Ensure a unified visual and interaction experience across iOS, Android, and Web — respecting platform-specific behaviors without fracturing the design system

Education & Experience

• 5+ years of experience in UX/UI and product design, with at least 2 years designing for mobile (iOS/Android) at a consumer product company

Must Demonstrate

• Understanding of color as a functional system communicating status, identity, causality, and trust

• Proficiency in Figma or equivalent — component libraries, auto-layout, design tokens, prototyping, and developer handoff

• Proficiency in motion/animation tools (Lottie, After Effects, Framer, or equivalent) with demonstrated ability to spec animations for engineering implementation

• Comfort with AI-assisted development tools such as Lovable, Cursor, or similar, and willingness to adopt new tooling quickly

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience designing for health, fitness, performance, or biomarker applications

• Experience designing consumer commerce surfaces in a trust-sensitive context, including in-app purchases, subscription tier presentations, or health/telehealth marketplaces

• Familiarity with React Native / Expo design constraints: safe areas, platform-specific scroll physics, gesture models, and native component behavior

• Light front-end knowledge (TypeScript, React Native, CSS) sufficient to assess implementation fidelity and communicate specific divergence from design intent

• Experience designing gamification and progression systems: achievement states, streak mechanics, leaderboard displays, tier progression

• Familiarity with identity-adaptive or multi-theme design systems: real-time palette shifts, persona-keyed visual treatments, multi-tier token management

• Experience with cinematic or motion-heavy product moments (brand launch surfaces, product reveal animations, celebration states) and demonstrated ability to art-direct sound, motion, and timing together

Certifications

• Applicable certifications are a plus

Other (Travel, Work Environment, DoD 8570 Requirements, Administrative Notes, etc.)

• Fast-paced, milestone-driven startup environment with hard ship dates; role leverages AI-assisted development tools (Cursor, Lovable, and equivalents) to accelerate design and development velocity

We take pride in being part of the Disability Confident Scheme. This helps make sure you can be interviewed fairly if you have a disability, long term health condition, or are neurodiverse. If you'd like to apply and need adjustments made, you can let us know in your application.

About the Role

As a Senior UX Designer, you'll play a central role in shaping the user experience and design of digital products built for the healthcare marketing industry. You'll work hands-on to create intuitive, accessible, and empathetic experiences for websites and interactive pieces that serve patients, healthcare providers (HCPs), and caregivers.

You'll own end-to-end UX delivery for your assigned projects, with strategic oversight from the UX Director. On larger-scale engagements, you'll often partner with a Lead UX Designer, contributing both hands-on craft and design thinking. Your work directly impacts real people navigating complex health journeys, so you'll balance business goals, user needs, and regulatory realities in equal measure.

What you'll do

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End UX Design & Deliverables

Own the full UX lifecycle for your projects and produce the artifacts that move work from concept to launch, including:

• Information architecture — sitemaps, taxonomies, navigation models, and content structures.

• User flows & journey maps — mapping task paths, decision points, and multi-state experiences (e.g., HCP vs. patient, pre- vs. post-authentication).

• Wireframes — low- to high-fidelity wireframes that clearly communicate structure, hierarchy, and interaction.

• Interactive prototypes — clickable Figma prototypes for stakeholder review and usability testing.

• Interaction & responsive design — detailed interaction specs, states, and behavior across breakpoints and devices.

• Design specifications & developer handoff — annotated UX documentation that gives development teams what they need to build accurately.

• Accessibility annotations — WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA guidance including focus order, keyboard navigation, ARIA intent, and inclusive design considerations built in from the start.

• Regulated content structure — designing experiences that accommodate compliance requirements such as fair balance, ISI placement, and referencing, in partnership with medical/regulatory reviewers.

• Design QA — reviewing built experiences against design intent and flagging discrepancies.

• UX Design system contributions — building, extending, and maintaining reusable components and patterns to keep work consistent and efficient.

User Research & Usability Testing

• Plan and conduct user research and usability testing sessions.

• Synthesize qualitative and quantitative findings into clear, actionable insights.

• Incorporate findings into UX iterations to ensure experiences are intuitive, accessible, and engaging while meeting user needs and business goals.

• Use research and analytics to validate design decisions and measure success.

Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration

• Partner closely with strategy, creative, copy, account, and development teams to translate complex requirements into intuitive solutions.

• Serve as a key advisor to creative teams on accessibility and compliance standards.

• Act as a critical bridge between user needs, business goals, and technical feasibility.

• Navigate regulated review workflows (e.g., MLR/PRB), designing in a way that anticipates and supports the review process.

Client & Stakeholder Communication

• Confidently present design concepts to clients and internal stakeholders.

• Clearly articulate design choices and their strategic impact on user outcomes and business goals.

• Facilitate workshops and design discussions and tell a compelling story through your work.

AI-Enabled Workflow

• Comfortably integrate AI tools into the design process — accelerating research synthesis, ideation, content drafting, prototyping, and documentation — while maintaining strong craft, critical judgment, and quality control.

• Stay curious about emerging AI capabilities and help the team identify where they add genuine value to UX outcomes.

About you

Qualifications

Required

• 8+ years of UX/product design experience, including leading design on projects end to end.

• A strong portfolio demonstrating full-lifecycle UX work — research, IA, wireframes, prototypes, and shipped experiences — across responsive web and interactive platforms.

• Proficiency in Figma, including prototyping and component/design-system workflows.

• Deep working knowledge of accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA) and inclusive design practices.

• Solid grasp of visual design fundamentals (typography, color, layout, hierarchy).

• Demonstrated experience planning, running, and synthesizing user research and usability testing.

• Proficiency with UX/product analytics tools (e.g., GA4, Hotjar) to inform and measure design.

• Excellent presentation and communication skills, with comfort presenting to and defending decisions in front of clients.

• Comfort integrating AI tools into a modern design workflow.

Preferred

• Experience in life sciences, pharmaceutical, or medical communications is a significant plus.

• Familiarity with regulated review processes (MLR/PRB) and compliant design considerations (fair balance, ISI placement, referencing).

• Experience designing HCP- and patient-facing digital experiences.

Casino & Sportsbook UI/UX Designer

Share

Post

Copy

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a hands-on Product UI/UX Designer to shape the player-facing experience of a B2C casino and sportsbook across desktop and mobile web. This is a long-term product design role—not front-end development, slot-game illustration, or banner-only production.

CREATIVITY IS THE CORE OF THIS ROLE

We need someone who can originate distinctive visual concepts, not simply rearrange templates. You should be able to take a product brief, explore multiple directions, explain your decisions, and turn the strongest idea into a cohesive, intuitive interface.

Our design direction is clean, premium, familiar, and comfortable to use. We value thoughtful typography, spacing, hierarchy, reusable components, subtle motion, and strong attention to detail. The product includes Korean-language layouts, but Korean fluency is not required.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Propose original visual directions and interaction ideas that give the product a recognizable identity.

• Design responsive homepages, casino lobbies, game cards, search, filters, promotions, and navigation.

• Design sportsbook event lists, odds displays, markets, live states, and bet-slip interactions.

• Improve sign-up, account, wallet, transaction history, notifications, messages, and promotion screens.

• Turn user flows into polished screens, interactive prototypes, and reusable Figma components.

• Define desktop/mobile behavior and hover, focus, selected, disabled, loading, empty, and error states.

• Collaborate with the product owner and developers on implementation details and visual QA.

• Occasionally support promotional banners and lightweight UI motion; product UI remains the primary focus.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

• Strong creative judgment and a portfolio showing original concepts, exploration, and polished execution.

• 2+ years of hands-on web or product UI/UX design experience.

• At least one relevant casino OR sportsbook website project; experience in both is a plus.

• Strong Figma skills: Auto Layout, components, variants, variables/styles, prototypes, and organized developer handoff.

• Solid responsive design, typography, information hierarchy, and interaction design skills.

• Working English for written communication and design discussions.

• Ability to explain exactly what you personally owned and why you made key design decisions.

NICE TO HAVE

• Experience with Korean or other Asian-market consumer interfaces.

• Design systems for content-rich products.

• Micro-interaction prototypes, subtle motion, or promotional banner design.

• Basic understanding of HTML/CSS constraints; coding is not required.

ENGAGEMENT

• Long-term, fully remote contract with full-time-equivalent availability.

• Monthly compensation: USD 1,500–2,000, depending on portfolio quality and relevant experience.

• Candidates worldwide are welcome; working-hour overlap can be discussed.

• Shortlisted candidates may be invited to a small paid trial before the long-term engagement.

HOW TO APPLY

Share 1–3 relevant projects and briefly explain:

1. Which screens, components, and design decisions you personally owned.

2. One original idea you introduced, the alternatives you explored, and why you chose the final direction.

3. Your experience with casino lobbies, sportsbook odds/markets, bet slips, wallets, or other relevant flows.

4. Your availability and expected monthly compensation.

Desktop/mobile examples and an NDA-safe Figma walkthrough are welcome. AI-assisted work is acceptable, but you must demonstrate your own design decisions and editable, production-ready work. Generic templates, banner-only portfolios, and AI-generated screenshots alone are not sufficient.

jd.1b9da1210dd84b5d:
Join IMP, a fast-growing B2B SaaS company focused on helping Multi-Academy Trusts (MATs) take control of their finances. As a Product Designer, you'll work closely with product squads, leading the design process from concept generation to usability testing and iteration. You'll have high autonomy and the opportunity to shape the design of established and next-generation products.

Job Title:

Product Designer - B2B SaaS

Salary:

£50,000 - £60,000

About IMP

At IMP we help Multi-Academy Trusts (MATs) take control of their finances. Our MAT-first software is built by people who know the sector inside out. Former trust professionals, finance experts and product specialists are all part of our team. More than half of all MATs in the UK already use IMP to plan with confidence, simplify complex processes and make smarter decisions.

We’re proud to be independent, founder-led and growing fast. Alongside our award-winning products, we’ve built a culture we’re equally proud of. We are ranked as one of the UK’s Top 25 Great Places to Work for mid-sized companies. Respect, collaboration and personal growth sit at the heart of how we work. You’ll find flexibility, support and opportunities to develop here, alongside regular team socials and funded CPD.

The role

We’re looking for a Product Designer to support our product squads and help grow our design operations.

You’ll be the only designer in the squads you support, taking prioritised requirements through divergent concepts, testing, iteration and convergence to something shipped and working in front of real finance teams - and you’ll stay with it through build. You’ll set the pace, make the calls, and bring engineering and product with you.

You will be one of two designers at IMP, working directly with our Head of Product Design. That is a deliberately small function: high autonomy, a short line to every decision, and nothing between you and the work. You will not be managing anyone.

Why this role is unusual

IMP is entering one of the most ambitious periods of product work in its history - the kind that comes round once in a company’s life, and rarely at one small enough that a single designer can leave fingerprints all over it.

To set us up for this transition, we’re re-writing our design playbook and using it to influence the design of our established and next-generation greenfield products. It’s the design platform we always dreamed about building: prioritising human creativity, exploiting AI tooling to help with drudgery and knowledge plumbing, and supercharging our output quality so we punch above our weight. You’ll be helping to shape all this. A couple of notable areas we’ve been developing recently:

•

IMPDesign.one

- our unified design system, spanning every product in the suite, generated and maintained by AI, human in the loop at every critical point.

•

IMPDesign.skills - A suite of AI-powered design skills built to remove the least interesting parts of the job - while leaving the thinking, the judgement and the craft entirely ours.

•

IMPInsight - A new insight platform for managing user feedback, allowing us to better understand our users’ needs, better test our assumptions and spend more time interpreting and using evidence in our craft.

That combination is rare: design work that reshapes software already critically relied on by real finance teams, building next-gen design operations at the forefront of the industry and working on greenfield concepts that grow our product suite.

And we strongly believe we’ve found the right balance between human creativity and AI tooling support – so if you’ve been using or experimenting with generative AI in your own practice and want somewhere that will fund it, take it seriously and let you push it further, this is unusually good ground.

What you'll own

No surprises here, but just to be explicit: your squads’ Product Owners run the discovery research that decides which user needs we address and in what order. From the point those prioritised requirements land, the design is yours:

•

Concept generation. Diverge first. Turn requirements into multiple concept variants that open the problem up and get teams thinking.

•

Usability testing. Test concepts with real users and our in-house domain experts - colleagues who have run MAT finance first-hand.

•

Collecting feedback + iterating. Fold the feedback back in, and support the squad in landing on a final solution everyone understands and you can defend.

•

Stay with it through build. Support the team through story breakdown and technical refinement, so what ships is what was agreed.

But you won’t be on your own:

•

Domain experts on-hand: You’ll be supported by stupendously knowledgeable product owners and product specialists helping you get the domain knowledge nailed.

•

Peer review, No donuts - You’ll be able to bounce ideas off and do peer reviews with the head of design (who designs our other products). And you’ll be working in a team of people who literally embody our company principle of “Don’t be a donut” who will treat you with respect and dignity and expect the same in return.

•

Regular planning, coaching and mentoring – You’ll be expected to manage your own work, but we have two dedicated sessions every week: one at the beginning to help plan your week, and one at the end to focus on you, your wellbeing and helping with any coaching and mentoring you’d like support with.

What we need from you

Essential

•

You've been the design lead on a squad or team - the only designer in the room, making the call. You can walk us through a real piece of work from requirement to shipped software and show us your decisions along the way.

•

You're a self-starter. Remote, embedded, sole designer: nobody is going to sequence your week for you.

•

You use generative AI in your design practice, or you've been actively exploring it. We don’t need you to be an expert - we need real curiosity and evidence you have tried things. You aren’t afraid to dabble in the Terminal. You’re experimental. Come ready to show us what you have built, broken or learned.

•

You design well for complex, data-dense products, and you write clearly enough that a remote team can follow your reasoning without a meeting.

•

A portfolio that shows your thinking and your process, not just the final screens.

Nice to have

•

Experience with accounting, finance or budgeting software.

•

B2B SaaS experience, particularly where users are professionals doing serious work under time pressure.

•

Experience designing interfaces on top of AI output - review states, confidence, correction, human-in-the-loop.

•

Experience designing across a multi-product platform or suite, rather than a single application.

•

Public-sector, education or otherwise regulated-domain experience.

Benefits:

•

27 days of holiday per year plus bank holidays (with a buy option up to an additional 5 days)

•

Enhance Maternity and Paternity leave

•

AXA Health insurance including dental, optical and mental health

•

Broadband allowance

•

Home office stipend

•

Life assurance (4 x basic salary)

•

Encouraged and funded CPD

Relevant experience helps, but we know the best candidates can come from varied backgrounds. We want to hear how your past work aligns with the work you’ll be doing at CutTime.

What it’s like to work with us

CutTime is a small and mighty company, and we know how to do a lot with a little. You’ll be the first design hire reporting directly to our Head of UX and collaborating closely with 4-5 engineers, our Head of Engineering, and our product manager. While we care a lot about our customers, we put our team first.

•
You’ll have the support you need balanced with the autonomy to structure your work in a way that best suits you.

•
You’ll be part of a collaborative and engaged cross-functional team. While our design team is small, you’ll have plenty of people around you to sharpen your thinking, provide feedback, and pair on problems.

•
We value focused work. Most of your time will be spent doing research and design.

•
As a team, we value accountability over availability while staying highly collaborative. We often use Slack, Gather, Linear, and Loom to communicate our ideas async without expecting responses immediately.

•
Each week, you’ll participate in a research standup and a 1:1 with our Head of UX, but we’ll leave it up to you to decide what other meetings you need to move work forward.

•
We care about a healthy work-life balance. You won’t be working more than 40 hours a week except during the rarest of emergencies.

•
Work stays at work. We don’t expect you to have Slack on your phone or answer email during your off hours.

What we offer

For full-time employees based in the United States:

•
Salary range: $140k-150k depending on experience

•
3 weeks paid vacation, plus 13 paid holidays

•
$4,000 annual office stipend

•
Health coverage through an HRA

•
Basic life and short-term disability insurance

•
401(k) with company match

•
Remote-first with no required commute

Our hiring process

Our hiring process is designed to give us the best sense of who you are, your relevant past experience, and how you think through problems without being overly demanding of your time. We know interviewing can be a stressful, long process, so we don’t require white boarding, take-home assignments, or all-day on-site interviews.

1. Application

You submit your resume and portfolio and fill out a short questionnaire. Our team reviews each one and will reach out if you’re selected for the next round.

2. Non-technical interview (30 min)

If we choose to move forward, we’ll follow up with a 30-minute non-technical call where we can learn about your background, what you’re looking for, and whether the role may be a good fit for both sides.

3. Past work presentation (45 min)

You’ll present some of your past work with a focus on your design process, how you solve problems and overcome challenges, and how you communicate and collaborate with a cross-functional team. We would like to see something beyond just a walk through of your portfolio, ideally a presentation deck with 1-2 polished case studies.

4. App critique (30 min)

We’ll ask you to critique an app to get a sense of how you think about product, systems, and visual craft, as well as how you prioritize and communicate. At the start of the interview, we’ll provide you with a Figma file containing a flow from an app we’ve selected and ask you to share your screen during the critique.

5. Decision and offer

Our team will review your materials and scores from each interview round. If you’re selected, we’ll extend an offer, discuss logistics, and give you time to decide.

Description

Position at ARRISE

ABOUT THE ROLE
We are building out our design capability for the tools that power our business from the inside out — platform, live casino, and studio operations, as well as the tools our operator partners use directly. This isn't about designing for players. It's about designing for scale. When thousands of people rely on the same workflow every single day, a small improvement — shaving a few clicks off a repetitive task, clarifying a confusing status flow — adds up to a massive impact across the business. If you love the kind of design work where the ROI is measurable and the problems are real, this is that role. A well-designed workflow here doesn't just look good; it removes friction at scale. Small improvements compound fast when they're used constantly, by many people, every single day. You'll work across platform, live casino, and studio tooling depending on the project, partnering closely with product, engineering, and a design team that spans Europe and India. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING
• Own the design of internal and operator-facing tools end to end — from a vague problem statement through to delivery-ready specs.

• Take ambiguous, undefined business problems and turn them into clear design direction — often with no existing brief or precedent to lean on.

• Spot when a problem isn't a one-off — and build systemic solutions instead of patching the same issue over and over.

• Set your own success metrics. Track task time, usage, and adoption, and let real data — not opinion — drive your decisions.

• Build and scale a design system that grows with a widening product surface.

• Present your thinking regularly to stakeholders and defend your rationale under real scrutiny.

• Work directly with the engineers and PMs who bring your designs to life.

• Help shape direction for other designers touching the same products — no formal authority required, just clear thinking and good instincts.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
Communication is critical to this role. You'll be presenting, aligning, and defending design thinking on a near-daily basis — with product, engineering, operations stakeholders, and fellow designers. We're looking for someone who can:
• Communicate clearly and concisely, with a defined point and structure — not open-ended or rambling

• Respond to challenge or new information with openness and adaptability, not defensiveness

• Manage stakeholders and cross-functional relationships independently, without needing a hand held — with the executive presence to be trusted in the room.

Beyond communication, you'll bring:
• Systems and workflow thinking — You naturally zoom out from a single screen to the workflow it's part of — and design for scale, not just for the task in front of you.

• UX-led craft. You don't need to be the sharpest visual designer in the room, but you do need real UX instincts: setting KPIs, reading usage data, letting behavior — not assumption — guide your decisions. Solid UI and design-system fluency are a given.

• A high tolerance for ambiguity. No brief? No problem. You can define the problem yourself, scope it, and get moving — this matters more here than in almost any other design role.

• Genuine curiosity. A real drive to make things better, not just familiarity with tools — Figma is a given, and openness to new tools (including AI-assisted workflows) is a good signal of that mindset, but the curiosity itself is what we're after. We want people with opinions, not just preferences.

** Prior iGaming experience is not required , and we're actively encouraging designers without it to apply. We're especially interested in candidates from B2B or SaaS environments, where working directly with business customers — and navigating ambiguity without a pre-defined brief — tends to be the norm rather than the exception. We're not looking for someone who checks every box perfectly. We're looking for someone strong and well-rounded across all of the above, with communication and ambiguity tolerance as the areas we weight most heavily.

ABOUT ARRISE
ARRISE sets the benchmark for service delivery and excellence in the iGaming industry. Playing a key role in the success of its clients, ARRISE helps to deliver exceptional gaming experiences to millions of players worldwide. 
Our global team of over 11,000 talented and driven professionals are shaping the future of iGaming. Headquartered in Gibraltar, we have offices spanning Canada, India, the Isle of Man, Latvia, Malta, Romania, Serbia, Bulgaria, and the UAE, and more exciting destinations on the horizon. 
At ARRISE, we take pride in creating growth opportunities at all levels, constantly investing in our people while welcoming new colleagues and forging strategic partnerships that open new opportunities for success.  To achieve this, we bet on ourselves. We know that success is a collective effort, and our team is driven by ambition, collaboration, and a shared commitment to grow and succeed — while embracing every step of the journey. 
Be part of the future of iGaming with 11,000 ARRISERS! See a job that excites you? Apply now, and our friendly recruitment team will connect with you soon. Your journey starts here.

• Experience designing conversational UI, chat interfaces, or AI copilot surfaces.
