Objection is building the truth infrastructure for the next century: fast, adversarial, AI-native adjudication at civilizational scale.

We are creating a platform for structured dispute resolution — adversarial fact-checking with ELO-rated participants, AI-assisted evidentiary analysis, and transparent methodology. We operate with complete editorial and institutional independence.

We run on a deliberate cadence: three weeks per month fully distributed, asynchronous, deep work; one week per month mandatory in-person for alignment, architectural debates, and strategic decisions. When remote, we operate on GMT time.

Each month, the company meets in the city we believe is the best at that time of year. Our current rotation includes Nassau (winter), New York City (spring and autumn), and London/Europe (summer). We follow seasonality and intensity. Strategy in Nassau. Commercial tempo in NYC. Institutional engagement cycles in Europe.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a product designer to architect the comprehensive user experience for Objection’s media claims dispute resolution platform. The interface must guide users through complex adversarial adjudication processes with confidence, clarity, and institutional trust — and the designer must build it with AI-native tools and workflows from the ground up.

This is not a conventional UX role. You will translate intricate procedural workflows and legalistic frameworks into seamless, frictionless digital interactions. You will minimize cognitive load for users engaging with a system designed to resolve disputes through structured argumentation, evidence evaluation, and AI-assisted adjudication.

This role is suited for professionals accustomed to:

•
Designing for complex, high-stakes, process-heavy products where clarity is non-negotiable

•
Transforming dense procedural or legal logic into intuitive user flows

•
Using AI tooling and agentic workflows to accelerate and augment design output

•
Working autonomously with structured written communication in distributed teams

The Role

As an Agentic Product Designer, you will:

•
Design the end-to-end user experience for Objection’s adversarial adjudication platform — from claim submission through tribunal output

•
Transform complex procedural workflows into seamless, frictionless digital interactions that minimize cognitive load

•
Establish a premium, high-trust visual language that reflects the institutional gravity of the platform

•
Develop and maintain a robust, scalable design system that ensures consistency across the entire product and accelerates development velocity

•
Conduct rigorous user research and usability testing to iterate on designs and solve real-world friction points

•
Partner closely with engineering and product management to ensure design fidelity is maintained from prototype to production

•
Embed inclusive design principles into the core of the product, ensuring the platform is universally accessible and equitable

•
Leverage AI-native design tools and agentic workflows to increase output, accelerate iteration, and systematize design operations

Who You Are

Required Experience

Professional product design experience with a strong portfolio in complex, data-rich, or process-heavy digital products. Demonstrated ability to take a product’s UX from architecture through to production-ready design.

Core Competencies

•
Deep empathy for the user, combined with the ability to impose clarity on complex systems

•
Precision in UI craft — you approach visual design with the rigor of an engineer and the sensibility of an artist

•
Systems thinking — you design for scalability, edge cases, and procedural integrity, not just the happy path

•
Fluency with AI-native design tools and a bias toward automating and systematizing design workflows

•
Comfort working autonomously in a distributed, asynchronous environment with clear written output

•
Experience pairing with developers to ensure implementation fidelity

•
Strong commitment to accessibility and inclusive design

A background in legal, fintech, govtech, or other high-trust, process-heavy domains is a strong advantage — but design instinct and rigor matter more than sector tenure.

•
Not a brand-only or marketing design role

•
Not wireframing to someone else’s specification

•
Not visual polish applied after the product is built

•
Not a role where AI tooling is optional

This is designing the environment in which truth is adjudicated. The UX is the product. And the designer builds with AI, not around it.

Fully remote, with mandatory monthly in-person summits in rotating global cities (Nassau, NYC, London/Europe)

Round-trip flights, hotel accommodation, and structured summit programming provided

•
Meaningful equity grants and annual performance bonus

•
We will calibrate seniority and scope to the right candidate

Good visuals are appealing to the eye, but great visuals tell stories that reignite your desire to discover, spark your creative imagination and even influence what we buy, eat, and do. That’s why CrowdRiff exists: to empower destination marketers to showcase their unique destinations through powerful visual storytelling solutions.

✨ CrowdRiff is built around the idea of pushing the boundaries of exploration; and our dedication to finding experiences that feel more authentic and undiscovered make us who we are. We like to think of ourselves as modern-day explorers, who believe in taking action now and thrive in an open, challenging, and encouraging environment.

Our team is a quirky and diverse crew that has one thing in common: our love for great visuals. Picture this. You will contribute to amplifying unique travel experiences like scuba diving in Tahiti 🌊, exploring Napa’s wine country🥂, bungee jumping in Queenstown 🤩and much more while having access to some of our amazing travel perks that allow you to immerse yourselves in local communities and culture.

Every day, we work across departments, time zones, and even oceans to reach our goals and delight our customers - all while being remote. If you are looking to make travel an incredible experience today, and for future generations, and are passionate about visuals & tech, you’re just our type. 💯

Your role: Senior Product Designer

Product design is changing fast.The best designers today don't wait for fully formed briefs. They talk to customers, identify problems, shape solutions, and move fast. They use AI as a force multiplier to prototype faster, synthesize insight at scale, and close the gap between what they imagine and what they put in front of a user.

At CrowdRiff, you will own a product area end-to-end, working closely with a PM and engineering team as a co-owner of product direction. You will often operate where the problem space is not fully defined. You are comfortable bringing structure, not waiting for it.

If you want to own meaningful product areas, move fast, and do some of the strongest product thinking of your career, this role is built for you.

What you'll be working on:

CrowdRiff builds software for destination marketers - the teams behind tourism boards, travel brands, and the organizations that help people discover and experience places. Our platform helps them plan content, manage their media, and tell better stories across every channel.

Our products are evolving quickly and the design problems you'll be working on include:

• Making complex, multi-step planning workflows feel intuitive for people who live in spreadsheets today

• Introducing AI-powered features that actually change how marketers work. Not bolt-on additions, but experiences that earn their place in the product

• Designing across surfaces where there's no established playbook yet. New interaction patterns, new user behaviors, new ways of thinking about what the product should be

• Unifying a platform that touches multiple workflows and user types, where coherence and clarity are ongoing design challenges

What you'll do:

• Own end-to-end design for your product area, from discovery through to shipped product

• Work as an embedded partner with your PM and engineering team, shaping direction early and validating ideas before investing in detailed design

• Talk to customers regularly and bring those insights directly into the design process

• Use AI tools actively throughout your workflow to synthesize research, generate early concepts, and prototype solutions quickly

• Identify conceptual gaps and usability challenges early, before development begins

• Translate user needs, business priorities, and technical constraints into scalable solutions

• Communicate design decisions clearly with stakeholders across product, engineering, and leadership

• Contribute to a design culture that values craft, rigour, and cross-functional partnership

What you'll bring:

• Experience leading design for a major product area, balancing user needs with business goals and technical constraints

• Strong foundations in UX, information architecture, and interaction design

• A natural instinct for workflow thinking. You spot conceptual gaps and edge cases before they become problems

• Strong product judgment. You know when to go deep, when to move fast, and how to make the right tradeoffs

• A portfolio that demonstrates product thinking and clear design rationale across end-to-end projects

• Comfort navigating ambiguity and the ability to build structure where it doesn't yet exist

• B2B SaaS experience is a strong asset

You might be a great fit if...

• You've used AI tools (Claude, Cursor, Figma Make, Paper, or others) to build something you wouldn't have attempted before

• You've found yourself closing the gap between design and the final product, and you're excited by where that's going

• You've operated where the problem wasn't handed to you, and that felt like an opportunity

• You have opinions about what something should feel like, and you can articulate why

$150,000 - $180,000 a year

The Senior UX Designer - Origination & Servicing, is responsible for designing intuitive, scalable, and compliant user experiences across Unlock’s most complex workflows, including lending-like processes such as application flows, eligibility determination, document collection, underwriting support, servicing, and settlement flows. Deep expertise in interaction design, systems thinking, and workflow mapping is essential, with less emphasis on visual/UI design. • Translate regulatory and business rules (e.g., eligibility constraints, pricing logic, disclosures, servicing requirements) into coherent user flows and system interactions.

• Design end-to-end journeys for homeowners, internal teams (Servicing, Underwriting, Post-Closing), and external partners.

• Produce wireframes, service blueprints, journey maps, prototypes, and usability test plans to guide product decisions.

• Partner with Product Managers to refine requirements, validate assumptions, and define success criteria for new workflows and platform capabilities.

• Conduct usability testing and synthesize feedback to iterate on flows, patterns, and information architecture.

• Collaborate with Engineering to ensure feasibility, consistent interaction patterns, and accessibility compliance.

• Advocate for UX standards and design thinking across teams, ensuring consistency and predictability in how complex rules and data are presented.

• Support modernization of internal systems (e.g., Badger 2.0, underwriting tools, servicing workflows) by simplifying dated or fragmented processes.

• 3–8 years of professional UX design experience, with emphasis on complex workflows, financial systems, enterprise tools, or regulated products.

• Experience conducting user research, usability testing, and synthesizing findings into actionable design recommendations.

• Proficiency with prototyping and design tools (Figma preferred).

• Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, Compliance, and Operations stakeholders.

• Ability to break down ambiguous problems and produce structured, testable UX solutions.

• Interest in leveraging AI in the design process

• PC skills including working knowledge of the Microsoft environment and the ability to access, manipulate, organize and relay information in a meaningful way.

• Excellent communication and relationship-building skills to effectively partner with leaders across multiple functions

• Experience leveraging AI in the design process

• Experience designing for mortgage, home equity, lending, or fintech products.

• Familiarity with underwriting workflows, disclosures, document management, or servicing platforms.

• Experience designing internal tools for operations teams.

• Understanding of accessibility standards (WCAG) and compliance-sensitive UX requirements.

• Experience with data-heavy interfaces, dashboards, or rule-driven decision tools.

• Flexible work arrangements and a strong emphasis on work-life balance

You will be joining the Monetization Products team, which builds the tools and experiences that help game developers and publishers grow their revenue — from in-game shops and checkout flows to partner-facing self-service products. About You

You are a Senior UX/UI Designer with strong UI and UX skills, capable of designing clear and scalable product experiences. You work at the intersection of product, business, communication design and engineering.

You actively use AI in your work and build AI-driven workflows (prompt → pipeline → automation) together with engineers. You’re comfortable working with complexity and unclear inputs.

You understand that the best shop experiences of tomorrow will be built by designers who can both conceive and code them.

You design and prototype end-to-end user flows (from interfaces to supporting materials), and validate impact through experiments. You are hands-on: you move fast in Figma, can turn ideas into interactive demos, and you are comfortable preparing partner-facing materials — presentations, landing pages, and product explainer assets.

You don’t manage a team directly, but you own the quality of UX and the outcome of your solutions, and you naturally align business, design, and engineering around them.

AI Workflows & Vibe Coding

• Build and iterate AI-driven workflows (prompt → flow → result).

• Work with no-/low-code tooling where possible to reduce dependency on core development.

Rapid UX & Visual Communication

• Turn ideas into clear UX flows, wireframes, and high-fidelity mock-ups in Figma.

• Prepare interactive prototypes to convey product behavior, motion, and micro-interactions.

• Create partner-facing materials: product presentations, landing pages, one-pagers, infographics, and other supporting creatives for go-to-market and integrations.

Discovery, Research & Experimentation

• Contribute to discovery: interviews, JTBD, surveys, CJMs and help translate insights into product decisions.

• Validate solutions and hypotheses through quick tests and experiments.

• Collaborate with analytics to define success metrics and interpret experiment results.

Monetization UX

• Translate monetization and growth ideas into concrete UX changes, prototypes, and experiments.

Bridge Business ↔ Design ↔ Tech

• Translate business problems and partner needs into clear UX artifacts: flows, specs, clickable prototypes, and simple documentation.

• Work closely with engineers to ensure feasibility and a smooth path from prototype to production.

• Contribute to internal standards for AI-assisted workflows, UX quality, and visual consistency (without direct people-management).

Qualifications & Skills

• 5–7+ years in product / UX/UI design.

• Strong UI skills (visual clarity, hierarchy, attention to detail, able to structure and visually support partner-facing presentations, landing pages, one-pagers, and product explainers).

• Strong UX thinking (flows, structure, consistency, edge cases).

• Strong system thinking: ability to design connected product experiences, not just individual screens.

• Proven AI production experience: evaluating models and tools, building prompt + workflow pipelines, and shipping automated creatives or AI-assisted flows into real use.

• Hands-on prototyping: confident in Figma and able to build interactive prototypes in Framer / React / HTML / CSS — ideally comfortable using AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, v0, or similar) to prototype and build.

• A genuine passion for vibe coding and AI-assisted design, even if still developing these skills — someone actively building this muscle, not just aware of it.

• Research skills: experience contributing to discovery (interviews, JTBD, CJM), usability tests and surveys; able to synthesise insights into clear UX decisions.

• Analytics & experiments: comfortable framing hypotheses, reading experiment/A∕B-test results, and connecting UX changes to business metrics.

• Experience working in complex environments with multiple stakeholders.

• Strong written and verbal communication in English — able to communicate clearly and help align stakeholders around your solutions.

Good to Have

• Strong track record of designing and shipping D2C and F2P / in-app monetization experiences (shops, checkouts, promotions, LiveOps).

• Experience in the gaming industry or working with game developers / publishers.

• Familiarity with D2C shops, monetization mechanics, checkouts, or payments product design.

• Ability to write functional front-end code (HTML/CSS/JS) or work with AI coding tools to build design prototypes independently — the kind of designer who reaches for Claude Code before Figma when exploring a new idea.

• Deep craft in interaction design, motion, and design systems; experience contributing to or maintaining a design system.

• Broad understanding of modern product architecture (APIs, client–server patterns, microservices, cloud).

• Experience with no-code / low-code tools such as Webflow, Retool, Zapier, or similar.

• Experience in a fast-paced startup or scale-up environment.

• Familiarity with growth design principles (conversion optimisation, funnel analysis, pricing presentation).

• Additional language skills relevant to key markets (e.g. Russian, Malay, Chinese).

Clera is an AI-powered talent agent that connects 55,000+ tech professionals with VC-backed startups — not through job boards, but through intelligent, personalized outreach via email, iMessage, and WhatsApp. We've grown from $0 to over $1M ARR in six months, backed by 1984 Ventures, Deel Ventures, and angels from OpenAI, Sequoia, a16z, and LinkedIn.

Our product is the agent itself — and the surfaces where talent and companies interact with it. That's what you'd be designing.

What you'd work on

This is a product design role, not a marketing one. Expect projects like:

•
Designing new flows for how candidates experience AI-driven job matching (onboarding, preference setting, opportunity review)

•
Evolving the company-facing dashboard where startups manage pipeline, review talent, and track agent activity

•
Defining interaction patterns for a product where the AI is the primary actor and the UI supports oversight, not manual input

•
Translating complex data (match scores, engagement signals, funnel metrics) into interfaces that are clear without being dumbed down

•
Occasionally shaping net-new product concepts from zero — we move fast and test ideas quickly

How the work happens:

This is flexible and project-based — not a fixed weekly retainer. We'll scope work together in chunks, typically with async briefs and feedback via Slack/Figma. You'd work directly with our CTO and founding team. Some weeks might be 15+ hours during an intense sprint; others might be quiet. What makes someone great at this

•
You've designed product UI/UX for software companies — ideally B2B SaaS, marketplaces, or tools with meaningful complexity. You're not just making things pretty; you're making systems legible.

You think in flows and states, not just screens. You naturally consider empty states, error cases, loading, edge cases.

You can work from a rough brief or a conversation and produce something that moves the product forward — not a pixel-perfect mockup that took two weeks.

•
You're fluent in Figma. Bonus if you have opinions about design systems and component architecture.

•
You've freelanced before and know how to manage your own time, ask the right questions early, and flag blockers without being chased.

What we offer

•
Competitive project-based compensation (we'll discuss rate and scope together)

•
Real product ownership — your work ships to tens of thousands of users, not a backlog

•
A small, sharp team that doesn't do design-by-committee

•
Potential to grow into a larger role as Clera scales

G Goodbill is hiring Product Design Lead

TYPE Full Time CATEGORY Product Design LOCATION Remote Anywhere
This job post is over 2 months old and may no longer be available.

About Goodbill

At Goodbill, our mission is simple: drive down the cost of hospital care for everyone.

Americans and their employers spend nearly half a trillion dollars every year on hospital care, with a meaningful portion wasted on unnecessary services, billing errors, and administrative friction. Goodbill uses AI and software to remove those costs, identify overspending, and empower patients to actively participate in their care.

Our approach has been recognized widely. TIME Magazine named Goodbill one of the Best Inventions of 2023 , highlighting our ability to flag unnecessary services and negotiate waste out of hospital bills. Since then, we’ve expanded to serve over 5,000 employers and 250,000 patients , partnering deeply with TPAs to deliver savings upstream for self-funded plans.

Along the way, we’ve earned accolades like the BBB Spark Award and the Front CSAT Award (2025) for outstanding customer satisfaction, while drawing attention from national press. Backed by top venture firms including Eniac, Maveron, Founders’ Co-op, Reach Capital, and Liquid2 , we’re building the trusted infrastructure to make hospital care cost less.

About the role

We’re hiring a Product Design Lead to own the end-to-end design of everything Goodbill builds: from complex enterprise workflows used by healthcare administrators to simple, delightful consumer experiences that help patients understand and reduce their medical costs.

This is a foundational role. You'll inherit an early-stage Figma component library and transform it into a scalable design system. You'll work directly with our CTO and CEO (who currently serves as the product designer) to establish the design function, raise the bar on every surface of the product, and help shape Goodbill's evolving brand positioning. You'll design for 3–4 engineers shipping up to 20 times a day, which means your work needs to be clear, decisive, and fast enough to keep pace with a team that doesn't wait.

Goodbill sits at a rare intersection: enterprise-grade B2B tools that manage claims, automate financial assistance applications, and route complex workflows, alongside consumer UX that needs to feel as effortless as the best apps. You'll own both, roughly 50/50, and should be thrilled by the range.

We believe the best healthcare software should be the easiest software. Your job is to make complex things feel simple, or at least feel simple at first blush, for claims teams, patients, and everyone in between.

You will:

• Own product design end-to-end. From discovery and customer conversations through wireframes, prototypes, high-fidelity mocks, and production. You're responsible for the full arc. You'll talk to customers daily: joining sales calls, customer syncs, running user research, sitting in on support tickets, whatever it takes to build the right thing.

• Build the design system. Take our nascent Figma component library and turn it into a real system that is consistent, scalable, and opinionated enough to accelerate engineering throughput dramatically.

• Design for AI-native experiences. Rethink traditional healthcare workflows through the lens of what AI makes possible. You're not adding AI to existing patterns; you're designing new patterns that couldn't exist without it.

• Ship to production. Use AI-assisted development tools (we use Devin, but you're welcome to use Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or whatever you prefer) to take your designs from Figma to deployed code, even if incrementally. You'll be empowered and expected to close the gap between design and production yourself.

• Shape brand and positioning . Goodbill's visual identity is always evolving. You'll have a strong voice in where it goes, always ensuring we present a sharper, more intentional expression of who we are and where we're headed.

• Partner deeply with engineering, operations, and leadership. You'll report to our CTO and work closely with our CEO. You'll design alongside 3–4 engineers in a team that moves extremely fast. Your designs need to be clear enough to build from immediately and flexible enough to evolve as we learn.

You are:

• A systems thinker who sweats the pixels. You can hold the entire product in your head while obsessing over a 2px alignment issue. You see how a component decision cascades across five surfaces and you care about all of them.

• Ruthless about killing your darlings. You don't get emotionally attached to your work. You get attached to outcomes. If a better solution emerges, from a customer conversation, an engineer's suggestion, or your own second look, you move to it without ego.

• AI-fluent. You use AI tools daily for prototyping, production, and pixel-perfection. You understand what agentic AI products feel like and you design for them natively, not as an afterthought.

• Fast and decisive. You thrive in environments where speed matters. You know when a rough wireframe is the right artifact and when a polished prototype is worth the time. You default to shipping over perfecting.

• Customer-obsessed. You're not designing from your desk. You're on calls, reading tickets, watching sessions. You build empathy through direct contact, not assumptions.

• Comfortable with complexity. Healthcare is messy: regulatory requirements, EDI standards, insurance jargon, and emotionally-charged moments for patients. You're energized by the challenge of making all of that disappear behind a clean interface.

• A strong communicator. You can articulate design rationale to engineers, executives, and customers with equal clarity. You bring people along without slowing down.

• Collaborative. You’ll work closely with Product, Operations, Sales, and Client Success to design features that move real dollars in the healthcare system.

Bonus

• Experience designing in healthcare, fintech, or other regulated domains.

• Familiarity with healthcare billing, claims processing, or insurance administration.

• You've built or contributed to a design system from the ground up.

• You’ve worked in an early-stage startup (pre-seed/seed/Series A).

• You've shipped code to production using AI-assisted design and development tools.

Why Goodbill

• Massive problem, huge upside. Americans and employers spend nearly half a trillion dollars a year on hospital care — much of it wasted. We’re fixing that with AI and software.

• Recognition + traction. Named one of TIME’s Best Inventions of 2023 ; serving 5,000+ employers and 250,000 patients ; backed by top VCs (Eniac, Maveron, Founders’ Co-op, Reach Capital, Liquid2).

• Rare design range. You'll design enterprise admin tools and consumer experiences in the same week, possibly the same day. Few roles offer this breadth at this stage.

• Ground-floor impact. You're building the design function. Your decisions on systems, patterns, and brand will define Goodbill's product for years.

• Mission-driven team. We live our values: do it for the patient, lead without ego, be transparent, own it, move quickly, sweat the details.

We offer

• Competitive pay (cash and equity)

• Unlimited PTO (Seriously — it’s not an empty benefit. We work too hard for anything else.)

• Health, dental, and vision plans covered 100% for you and 50% for dependents

• A monthly fitness stipend

• Internet or co-working space stipend

• Primary care membership stipend

• Remote office equipment stipend

• Quarterly team retreats

Visit our About Us page to learn more about Goodbill , our mission, and what it’s like to work with us.

Goodbill, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.

The Role

We are looking for a fully remote Senior UX Designer to lead the complete rebuild of our core B2B contracting and administration platform. We are transitioning a legacy system into a modern, performant application using React, Tailwind, and Shadcn UI .

Your challenge is unique: Our users are experts in contracts and administration, not technology. They manage complex, high-stakes workflows, but they need an interface that feels simple, safe, and intuitive. You will bridge the gap between "powerful functionality" and "ease of use."

Why This Role Matters

Contracting and administration are historically dense, paper-heavy processes. You aren't just digitizing a form; you are orchestrating how our customers manage their business relationships. You will define how our "mid-enterprise" clients interact with the platform for the next 5-10 years, moving them from a legacy experience to a modern, component-driven interface.

What you will focus on first

You will lead the early rebuild of our core platform experiences, starting with navigation and information architecture, then moving into data-heavy reporting and inventory-style workflows, then expanding into core objects (people and documents), the transactional workflows that connect those objects, and finally supporting admin surfaces like settings, activity logs, and audit history.

This role is designed for someone who excels in complex B2B SaaS UX and component-based systems.

Key Responsibilities

Simplifying Complexity (The Core Challenge)

• Workflow Distillation: Take complex, multi-stage contracting lifecycles and distill them into linear, understandable user flows for non-technical users.

• Information Density: Design interfaces that can handle large amounts of data (lists, contract clauses, metadata) without overwhelming the user. You know when to use a table, when to use a card, and how to manage whitespace in a data-heavy B2B environment.

• Error Prevention: Design "guardrails" that prevent non-technical users from making critical errors in the administration process.

Design System & Engineering Collaboration

• Shadcn & Tailwind Implementation: You won't be building a design system from scratch. You will leverage and theme Shadcn UI components and Tailwind CSS . Your job is to apply these constraints creatively to build consistent, developer-friendly designs.

• Developer Hand-off: Work closely with frontend engineers. You understand the "box model" and can design in Figma with auto-layout in a way that translates 1:1 to React components.

• Design QA : Partner with Engineering during implementation to ensure the shipped experience matches design intent, resolving UX edge cases within technical constraints.

Research & Empathy

• User Advocacy: Our users are cross-functional teams, from sales agents and administrators to project stakeholders and executives. They are time-constrained, context-switch constantly, and need to move work forward with minimal training. You will conduct research to understand how each group organizes information, makes decisions, and completes key workflows, then map the UI to match that reality and reduce cognitive load.

• Legacy Migration: Help users transition from the legacy platform to the new system. Identify which workflows are must-haves versus clutter, then design the bridge to the new experience with clear patterns and minimal disruption.

Who You Are

• The Simplifier: You look at a screen with 50 inputs and instinctively know how to group, paginate, or progressively disclose them to make it approachable.

• The Component thinker: You don't just draw rectangles; you think in atoms, molecules, and organisms. You understand how a change to a button in the library affects the whole platform.

• The Pragmatist: You understand the balance between "pixel perfect" and "shipping value." You are comfortable using an existing library (Shadcn) to speed up development rather than reinventing standard patterns.

Qualifications

• Experience: 5+ years of Product Design experience, specifically in B2B SaaS or complex enterprise tools.

• Portfolio: Must show examples of workflow design , data tables, dashboards, or form-heavy interfaces.

• Technical Fluency: Strong familiarity with Atomic Design principles and experience designing for React/Tailwind environments. You don't need to code, but you need to know how the code works.

• Domain Experience: Experience in PropTech, LegalTech, HR Tech, ERPs, or Document Management systems is a massive plus.

Tech Stack Context for the Designer

• Design Tool: Figma (Auto-layout mastery required)

• Frontend Framework: React

• Styling/UI Library: Tailwind CSS / Shadcn UI

Please note: this is a fully remote, work-from-home position.

familiarize yourself with the product

getting familiar with, contribute and evolve our design system and designs

collaborate closely with PM and engineers

do QAs for the implemented designs

collaborate with another designer working on a different product of ours

communicate with other stakeholders

You’re comfortable using and contributing to an already existing design system

You are proficient in Figma

You’re great at listening and asking questions, a good communicator with solid (but by no means native) English skills

•
You should care about the quality of products we provide beyond delivering designs.

What we’re offering

•
$120,000–$160,000 USD/year depending on your experience

•
Generous benefits for US employees

•
We offer a 401(k) matching plan where GroupCollect, LLC matches 100% of your contributions up to 3% of your salary, and then 50% of your contributions on the next 2% of your salary.

•
Flexible Health Reimbursement Arrangement (HRA): more affordable than traditional group health plans, personalized to suit your unique healthcare needs, and nontaxable.

•
Ample paid time off: 30 days per year for international contractors; 20 days per year + 10 legal holidays for US employees (though you can trade legal holidays for days off if you want)

•
Unlimited paid sick leave

•
$4,000/year for any hardware, software, furniture, conferences, books, videos or courses you wish to purchase. Anything that will help you do a better job.

What it’s like to work with us

We are a bootstrapped company with a small and nimble crew. While we care a lot about our customers, we put our team first.

•
You’ll work in a relaxed, informal atmosphere which lets you focus on your work without getting in the way.

•
Most of your time will go into research and design, not meetings.

•
Your most impactful work will be structured as broader projects which take about two months to research, plan and design and another two months to build and release.

During the planning phases, you’ll have repeated check-ins with the product manager, the team lead and the project engineers.

Beyond that, you’ll have a short daily meeting with the team and informal conversations as needed.

Application :

The Mission

As the Product Manager UX Orchestration , you own the no-code configuration layer of the Actirise solution: the tools that let publishers activate ad formats, configure the video player, and set up the CMP/Paywall experience — without a single line of code. You are the guardian of a consistent, controlled self-serve experience across every surface: back-office, client-facing UI, native platform, and WordPress plugin alike.

Your mission: make configuration effortless for publishers while keeping Actirise in control of what's truly self-serve versus internally managed — turning orchestration into a growth lever, not an operational bottleneck.

Your key responsibilities:

1. No-Code Configuration Strategy

•
Define which configuration flows are self-serve vs. internally-managed, and design the framework that governs that boundary.

•
Own the roadmap for the tagging plan (ad format activation), enabling publishers to activate and manage formats without dev intervention.

•
Continuously simplify configuration paths — remove friction, reduce support tickets, increase adoption of self-serve tools.

2. Player & Video Catalog Configuration

•
Own the player template configuration experience: enable publishers to customize player behavior and appearance without engineering support.

•
Design and evolve the video catalog management tools (upload, organization, metadata) to keep the catalog scalable and easy to maintain.

3. CMP / Paywall Template Configuration

•
Own the CMP/Paywall template configuration layer to deliver an easy configuration experience that respects both constraints.

•
Ensure publishers can configure consent/paywall templates consistently, regardless of the surface they use.

4. Cross-Surface Consistency

•
Guarantee that the configuration experience is coherent whether accessed via back-office, client-facing platform, or the WordPress plugin.

•
Ensure design system application to keep configuration UI patterns consistent across surfaces.

•
Define and maintain clean data contracts and ACLs for every configuration action.

5. Agentic Exposure

•
Apply an agentic-first principle to every configuration capability: whatever a publisher or an internal user can do through the UI must also be executable by an AI agent not just clickable in a screen.

•
Continuously audit existing configuration flows to close the human/agent parity gap ("can an agent already do what a human can do here?") and prioritize closing the biggest gaps.

6. Cross-Functional Collaboration

•
Work closely with the Sparteo Account squad to ensure configuration is part of a smooth time-to-activation journey.

•
Coordinate with PM Engagement on shared UI/UX and compliance boundaries.

•
Partner with Tech/Engineering to ship configuration tools that are reliable, fast, and scalable.

PM Expertise: 3+ years of experience in Product Management, ideally on self-serve platforms, admin/back-office tools, or no-code/configuration products.

•
UX Sensibility: Strong instinct for simplifying complex configuration flows into intuitive, guided experiences. Comfortable partnering with design systems.

•
Technical Literacy: Understanding of API-first design, WordPress plugin environments. You don't need to code, but you need to speak engineering's language.

•
Systems Thinker: Able to design frameworks (self-serve vs. managed) rather than one-off features — you think in guardrails, permissions, and consistency across surfaces.

•
Cross-Functional Operator: Comfortable working at the intersection of multiple squads where boundaries require coordination, not competition.

•
Agentic Mindset : Naturally designs every capability with a dual interface in mind — human UI and agent-executable action. Understands agent tool-calling patterns and can define clean, well-scoped tool interfaces rather than exposing raw UI logic.

•
AdTech / Video Culture: Familiarity with ad format activation, video players, or CMP/consent tooling is a strong plus.

•
Communication: Excellent communication skills — you can align Tech, Design, and client-facing teams around a shared configuration vision.

•
A strategic thinker with an 'AI-native' reflex, you excel at deconstructing business complexity into flawless operational blueprints . You don't just use AI; you design the structured documentation and logic flows that allow intelligent systems to execute our vision with precision

UI Product Designer

About Us

Proton is building the AI operating system for wholesale distribution, embedded in the workflows that move nearly every physical product on the planet. Distribution is a $9 trillion industry running on software that has been stuck for decades. We unify CRM, PIM, eCommerce AI, and Order & Quote Entry AI into one platform with one data layer and one AI brain, so reps spend their time on customer relationships instead of data entry.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. Everyone here is a builder who owns problems end to end and ships AI-native software faster than anyone else in the category.

The median Proton customer reports 3x profit return per dollar spent and an extra day of sales per rep per month. Hundreds of distributors run on Proton, from family-owned shops to publicly-traded enterprises. We're backed by Felicis Ventures and Battery Ventures.

The Role

We're hiring a UI Product Designer to own how Proton looks and works. Reporting to the VP of Product, you'll ship in a squad with PMs and engineers, and you'll be in front of customers constantly, watching reps use what you built and bringing back what you can only learn in person. Our product people know their users by name, not through a research summary.

Those users sit in one screen for eight hours a day and have spent their careers with software they merely tolerate. We want them to have something they'd choose: fast, modern, a pleasure to use. That's the hard version of the job, because most of the UI patterns you'd reach for by default were drawn for software that couldn't think. Ours can.

Two things make this role different from a standard product design opening:

• You're an AI-native designer, not just a Figma operator. Everyone here uses Claude Code and similar agentic tools as a first-class collaborator. We expect concepts prototyped in real code, put in front of people, and iterated with heavy AI leverage. Prototype before you polish, and make the calls AI can't.

• You set the craft bar. This hire decides how Proton looks and feels. Distribution software is famously grim and we intend to be the exception. You'll own the visual language and the design system across all four products.

Location : Cambridge, MA (hybrid, 3 days a week in Harvard Square) or remote in the EU.

Level : Product Designer through Senior Product Designer. Scope and autonomy change across that range.

Compensation : $80k – $100k base depending on experience, plus bonus, equity, and full benefits. EU offers are benchmarked to local market.

What You'll Do

• Prototype in code with Claude Code or Cursor to feel an interaction before we commit

• Own the design system: components, interactions, documentation, and the harder part, getting every squad to use them.

• Define what AI looks like here. Nobody has settled patterns yet, so you'll decide what it looks like when a rep trusts an agent and when they overrule one.

• Work inside our agentic scrum model. We don't run two-week sprints; cadence follows what a team and its agents can ship, and you'll help work out what design looks like in that.

• Get in front of customers constantly, including onsite. Distributors work in warehouses and on sales floors, and the best design calls come from standing next to a rep.

Requirements

• Craft that is demonstrably yours. Command of typography, layout, color, hierarchy, and iconography, with motion when it earns its place. You pull references from well outside software, and your work looks like someone made it rather than assembled it. We are explicitly not hiring people who let AI make their taste decisions. AI amplifies taste, it doesn't create it.

• Real end-to-end delivery. Shipped products, real users, real ownership, alongside PM and engineering. Hands-on work, not an LLM-generated portfolio.

• Daily, hands-on use of AI in your practice. Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent, used to ship real work rather than generate comps. You can say concretely how you structure context and check what comes back.

• A portfolio. Products or features you took from concept to launch where you set the visual language yourself. We're most interested in a workflow you found trapped in a legacy system and reimagined: what you kept, what you threw out, and how you got people to move.

• Systems thinking. You can author one beautiful screen and write the rules that let others make fifty consistent ones. You are curious enough to understand what's cheap to build and what isn't.

• Real agile experience, and a pull toward customers. You've worked inside traditional scrum and know what those rituals were for. We've replaced it with an agentic scrum, and knowing the original is what lets you help rebuild it. You'd also rather be in the room with a user than briefed about them.

Big Plus

• Complex B2B, enterprise, or ERP-adjacent software, with high-frequency users and workflows people can't opt out of.

• Agentic products, and the patterns for trust, correction, and handoff between a person and an agent.

• Early-stage SaaS startups.

Benefits

• Competitive salary + company stock options — we want you to feel like an owner.

• Flexible schedule with high autonomy.

• Unlimited PTO + 10 company-paid holidays.

• 12 weeks fully paid parental leave (primary and secondary, including adoption and fostering).

• Annual company-paid offsites.

Senior Product Designer - Embed

Reporting to: CTO

Location: Remote +/- 4hrs GMT

About Kota

Kota is making insurance and retirement benefits as accessible as modern software. We have two flagship products, the Kota Platform - the world's first fully integrated benefits platform and Kota Embed - our embedded insurance and retirement product for any platform.

Our mission is to make insurance and benefits more accessible and delightful to this generation of employees.

At Kota, we combine world class engineering with a strong sense of purpose. We build extraordinary user experiences, with curiosity and craftsmanship at the core of everything we do. If you want to work with modern tech, solve meaningful problems and be part of a team that truly cares, you should take a look.

Today, we power benefits for tens of thousands of employees at Europe's most forward-thinking companies, including Carwow, Tines, Zoe, and Remote. Founded in 2022, we've raised more than €20M from leading investors like EQT Ventures, Eurazeo, Northzone, and Frontline, along with founders and executives from Workday, Remote, Personio, OpenAI, and more.

Who are we looking for

Perfect for a senior who wants to think as part of the job (not just ship).

On Kota Embed you design a surface where a sort-order decision moves real money for tens of thousands of people, where the data model is co-designed with the UI, where 6–10 stakeholders are co-present in major decisions, where constraints become design surfaces rather than obstacles, where prototypes are spec, and where the work compounds into a body of named, citable patterns rather than dissolving into ad-hoc Figma files.

At this moment this is not a steady-state senior IC role. It's a "the ground is moving and you need to own the design quality while it does" role.

You need to want that, not just tolerate it.

What we are looking for

•
A designer who has worked inside a complex product (ideally B2B, double ideally it was API-driven), understands why the data model constrains the interface, and finds that constraint interesting rather than annoying.

•
You've shipped something with invisible complexity. Not a marketing site, not a dashboard with toggles. You succeeded, and you can explain how you thought through it.

•
Research methods at sprint cadence. 5-user tests, rapid Figma Make/Cursor/Paper prototyping, Datadog/Mixpanel log analysis, facilitating internal design reviews. You also know when to skip research and ship. The mantra: "rough data is better than no data; you can't remove uncertainty - triage it"

•
Outcomes-over-outputs discipline. Lock down problem / assumptions / success criteria before agreeing to a solution.

•
Systems thinking - promoting patterns to primitives. Recurring interaction surfaces become design-system components.

•
UX influence work. Getting devs/stakeholders to attend usability sessions. Building and facilitating ceremonies (standups, retros, backlog grooming) so design becomes shared team context, not an isolated artifact.

•
Craft fundamentals. Type, spacing, rhythm, hierarchy. The basics, worked at 400% zoom - quality and speed aren't opposites.

•
Builder craft. Cursor / Claude Code comfort. Treating prototypes as spec means producing working prototypes is the design output. Closing the gap between design and engineering rather than widening it.

Things you might know about or be interested in

•
Embedded financial products.

•
Fintech, financial services, insurance, or benefits platforms.

•
Developer product experiences, understanding of how to design for technical users and embedded/integration-heavy products.

Our values

•
Have Integrity. We care deeply about our why and it won’t jeopardise our how.

•
Care Deeply. Our products are our story, we look at the details, go the extra mile to delight customers.

•
Own Your Ship . Ask why, do the work, get the data, solve the problem, be an owner.

•
Raise the Bar . We continuously look to push past good enough. Expect more, move faster, and never stop raising your and the team’s standards.

•
Play to Win . We exist because we decided to say no to the norm – now we do this everyday.

And of course.... Your employee benefits!

•
Health Insurance contribution via Kota

•
Access to a Workplace Pension with matched contributions up to 5% via Kota

•
WFH stipend to support your home office needs

•
Group Life Assurance via Kota

•
Generous Paid Time Off - work hard and take the time you need

•
Annual, company-wide offsite

Our Hiring Process

•
Recruiter Screen: A 15-30-minute initial alignment conversation to understand f there is a match.

•
Intro call: A 30-minute 1-on-1 video call. We'll discuss Kota, your background, and your approach to collaboration and design systems.

•
Design deep-dive: A 60-90-minute call with our product and existing design team member to review portfolio work in detail, discuss design methodology, and work through a design systems challenge.

•
Culture call with founders: Chat with founders focused on culture and product thinking.

Set the visual and interaction quality bar across the product.

UX Research

Establish a structured research practice — define priorities, run interviews, surveys, and usability tests.

Translate raw research into prioritized, actionable product decisions.

Direct and level up the existing UX researcher on the team — provide structure, frameworks, and clear priorities.

Core Strengths (Must Have)

Data & Analytics

Deep experience with Mixpanel, GA4, Amplitude, or similar product analytics tools .

Experience designing and running A/B tests (GrowthBook, Optimizely, or similar) end-to-end.

Background in CRO (conversion rate optimization) or growth-driven design.

UX Research

Experience designing and running user interviews, surveys, and research frameworks.

Ability to translate research into clear, actionable product decisions.

You will define how UX drives growth, retention, and monetization at scale.

You will turn UX from a weak point into a competitive advantage .

We expect people to take initiative, move fast, and continuously improve the product.

Summary of the Role:

As a Product Designer at Maze, you'll define what product design looks like for AI agents in cybersecurity — a problem space where the design patterns don't exist yet. This is an early-hire role at a well-funded Series A startup building at the intersection of generative AI and security, and you'll own the product surface end-to-end while working directly with our Head of Product, engineering, and founders.

The product challenge is genuinely new. Our AI agents investigate vulnerabilities autonomously, surface findings with real context, and collaborate with security teams to cut through noise. Your job is to design how humans and agents work together — how trust gets built, how decisions get communicated, how complex security workflows become understandable. There's no playbook for this. You'll create one.

This role suits someone who operates closer to a product director than a screen-shipper — driving direction, influencing strategy, and making business-impact calls, alongside the visual craft to deliver them. You'll be using AI tools daily to move faster, but your craft is the floor: every design choice should hold up on its own merits, independent of how it was generated. Success looks like a design system shipped and adopted across the product, and concrete product outcomes — feature adoption, POC-to-customer conversion, and customer satisfaction with the experiences you ship.

Your Contribution:

•
Define AI-Agent UX Patterns: Design how security teams collaborate with autonomous AI agents — how investigations get presented, how trust is established, how humans steer the agent without slowing it down. You're inventing patterns, not applying existing ones.

•
Drive Product Direction, Not Just Design: Operate as a product-led designer — shaping roadmap, challenging requirements, influencing leadership with research and business reasoning. The bar is "what should we build, and why" alongside "how should it look."

•
Own the Product Surface End-to-End: Take features from problem framing through shipped product, working in tight partnership with PMs and engineers — including backend. Run discovery, prototype rapidly, validate with customers, and stay close to implementation. No throwing designs over the wall, no shipping around the engineering team.

•
Build the Design System: Create and scale a component-based design system that becomes the foundation for everything we ship. Establish patterns for AI-human collaboration that the team can build on as we grow.

•
Pioneer AI-Assisted Design Workflows: Use AI tools to accelerate ideation, prototyping, and exploration — and develop the methodologies the rest of the team will adopt. Your daily workflow is itself a contribution.

•
Translate Research Into Design: Run customer research, talk to security teams directly, and turn what you learn into shipped product. Use AI-assisted analysis to move from insight to prototype in days, not weeks.

•
Set the Quality Bar: Establish what "good" looks like for product design at Maze across craft, consistency, and customer impact — as the foundation for a design team that scales behind you.

What You Need to Be Successful:

•
Visual Craft for Data-Dense UI: A portfolio that holds up to detailed scrutiny — strong colour theory, deliberate visual hierarchy, considered information architecture for complex workflows. This is the bar, not a nice-to-have. Your interview will dig into specific design choices and why you made them.

•
Product Design Track Record: 4-7 years of professional product design experience, with shipped work in B2B SaaS. We're flexible on years; demonstrated craft and clear ownership matter more than time served.

•
Data-Heavy B2B Interfaces: Direct experience designing for complex workflows, dense data, and technical audiences. Dashboards, investigation tools, developer products, security platforms — the kind of UI where information density and decision support actually matter.

•
AI as Tool, Not Crutch: You use AI tools (Figma AI, Cursor, v0, Midjourney, ChatGPT/Claude, etc.) as part of your daily workflow and can speak credibly to what they're good for and where they break down. Critically, every design choice you ship should hold up on its own — AI accelerates your work, it doesn't substitute for foundational craft.

•
Product-Strategic Thinking: Track record of driving product direction, not just executing on briefs. You've influenced what to build with research, framed problems for leadership, and made business-impact calls — ideally in environments where you operated without a dedicated PM.

•
Deep Engineering Collaboration: Demonstrable history of shipping work in tight partnership with engineers — including backend. Pairing on implementation, working in design tokens, understanding the systems your designs land in, building consensus rather than shipping around resistance.

•
Design Systems Experience: Background building or meaningfully contributing to a design system in a production product. You think in components, tokens, and patterns, not one-off screens.

•
Customer-Led Approach: Comfortable running discovery directly with users, synthesising what you hear, and using that to make calls about what to build. You don't wait for research to be handed to you.

•
Nice to haves:

•
Experience designing for cybersecurity, developer tools, or other technical product domains

•
Background designing agentic or AI-native product experiences (not just AI features bolted onto existing products)

•
Early-stage startup experience where you've operated without a manager or established design function

Why Join Us:

•
Define a New Design Space: AI agents in security is a genuinely new problem. The interaction patterns, trust models, and workflows don't exist yet — you'll create them. The work you do here will influence how this entire category gets designed.

•
Fast-Track to Design Leadership: This is a founding-trajectory role and we're hiring for someone who wants a long-term home, not a stepping stone. As the team scales, the natural path is IC → Lead → Head of Design. If you have leadership ambitions, you'll have the runway to grow into them. If you'd rather stay deeply hands-on, the IC scope grows with the product.

•
Ambitious Challenge: We're using generative AI (LLMs and agents) to solve one of the most pressing problems in cybersecurity — the gap between vulnerability findings and meaningful action. You'll be designing at the cutting edge of this field.

•
Expert Team: Work alongside hands-on leaders with experience in Big Tech and Scale-ups. Our team has been part of the leadership teams behind multiple acquisitions and an IPO.

•
Impactful Work: Cybersecurity is a force for good. The experiences you design will directly affect how security teams protect organisations worldwide.

•
Build an AI-Native Company: We're building a new company in the AI era with the opportunity to design everything from the ground up — including how the design function itself works. You'll help pioneer AI-assisted design practices and set new standards.

Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

The role:

We’re looking for a Staff/Principal Product Designer to lead design for Synthesia’s core creation and editing experience: the surfaces where customers script, build, iterate, collaborate on, and publish videos at scale.

This area is central to redefining how video is created: removing the need for traditional editing while increasing the quality and consistency of what customers can produce.

You’ll operate as a senior IC: setting direction, influencing roadmap decisions (not just contributing), shaping bets with Product and Engineering leaders, and raising the craft bar across the entire creation experience - not just our editor.

We’re building a video creation platform for everyone, not a specialist tool. We see a future where Synthesia sits alongside word processors, presentation software, and spreadsheets as a staple used by many. That means we need to move beyond the prevailing paradigms of video creation and invent new ones that are powerful without being complex.

In practice, this role is about core editor / creation platform problems, for example:

•
Designing canvas + timeline/editor workflows that feel approachable on the surface and powerful in depth.

•
Creating repeatable interaction patterns that scale across the creation experience and help users build a consistent mental model

•
Improving creation quality through better structure, guidance, and feedback loops while users are building content.

•
Enabling collaboration and iteration inside the editor (reviews, handoffs, reusable patterns, consistency).

•
Working in a space where AI changes what “authoring” means, and the best patterns are still emerging.

In this role you will:

•
Own major creation/editor bets end-to-end, from problem framing to shipped outcomes and iteration.

•
Set a design vision for key parts of the editor, and influence adjacent product surfaces to stay coherent.

•
Partner closely with Product and Engineering to define what “great” looks like (principles, quality bar, success metrics) and then drive toward it

•
Prototype and test interaction models quickly (and know when high-fidelity matters).

•
Raise the bar on craft: interaction design, UI quality, systems thinking, and consistency across the creation experience.

You should apply if you bring

•
Significant experience designing complex, high-usage product surfaces (creation tools, editors, collaboration/canvas-based products).

•
Strong craft in interaction design and UI, and a track record of shipping work that measurably improves the product experience.

•
Comfort operating in ambiguity: you can turn unclear problem spaces into crisp direction, and you do not wait for perfect clarity.

•
Systems thinking: you understand how product architecture, state, and constraints shape the UX (not just the screens).

•
Excellent communication in design reviews and cross-functional decision-making contexts.

•
Leverage feedback from our users & customers to ensure our product continues to meet their needs.

•
Tackle complex and novel problems as we mature our nascent product and uncover new use cases.

•
Play a key role in the early stages of product development as part of a team that aspires to create one of the best designed SaaS tools out there.

•
Work with a team that ships fast and iterates quickly..

•
Solve our most important UX problems and shape the future of Synthesia - from the initial idea stage to the final execution.

At Synthesia we expect everyone to:

•
Put the Customer First

•
Own it & Go Direct

•
Be Fast & Experimental

•
Make the Journey Fun

A flexible, remote friendly role based out of Europe or one of our hubs in London, Copenhagen, Munich, or Zurich.

25 days of annual leave + public holidays in the country where you are based.

•
A generous referral scheme.

•
Work from home set up.

•
At Synthesia, you can work from anywhere ( within reason) in the world for up to 60 days per year!

•
A huge opportunity for career growth as you’ll help shape a market-defining product.

New features

in person a few times a year

Pay: €60.000 to €90.000 annually, adjusted by experience
and location

At Miaplaza, we build homeschool platforms that kids aged 4–18 actually
want to use — Miacademy, MiaPrep, and our Online High School are serving
over 150.000 students today. Our product foundations are strong. What we
want next is a step change in how our products feel: more expressive
illustration, more purposeful motion, more moments of craft that turn a
lesson into something a kid remembers.

We're hiring a Senior Product Designer whose craft anchor is illustration
and motion. Our design team is small and senior, five designers when you
join, and each brings a distinct strength: brand, design systems, research,
and now yours.

The role

You'd own product design for the student learning experience end-to-end:
from problem framing through delivery, in a Product Trio with a PM and EM
who have strong opinions and expect yours. This is product work with real
trade-offs — pedagogical, technical, and business — and you're accountable
for how it lands, not just how it looks.

Beyond Curriculum, you'd set the illustration and motion bar for all of
Miaplaza: the standards, motion principles, and character direction that
the other designers and the design system build from.

A defining part of the role is art-directing AI-assisted production. You'd
build the prompts, references, and review process that let a small team
produce quality illustration and motion at a scale hand-crafting alone
can't reach. We don't expect you to know every current tool — we expect the
taste and judgment to direct output rather than accept defaults.

You'd report to the Head of UX, with regular 1:1s covering craft, product,
and career growth. The direction is upward: deeper craft leadership,
cross-product influence, or both.

Job requirements

You must have all of these to be considered:

• A portfolio of shipped digital product work — not only concepts or standalone pieces

• At least 2 years working inside a product team, collaborating with PMs and engineers

• Strong illustration or motion skills, with at least 1 year focused on either as a primary craft

• Proficiency in Figma

• Some experience directing or guiding visual work produced by others — freelancers, junior designers, or AI tools

You’ll stand out if you also have:

• Deep motion skills in product contexts: interactions, transitions, onboarding, character animation

• Experience using AI image or motion tools as production accelerators

• Confidence running your own usability research, not just receiving findings

• Multi-brand or education-focused design experience

• Accessibility practice, especially for neurodivergent audiences

This probably isn’t right for you if:

• Your work hasn't yet lived inside a live product with real constraints

• You prefer well-scoped tasks over shaping ambiguous problems

• You see AI tools as either a threat to craft or a shortcut around it

Our hiring process

As a remote company, we receive a large number of applicants, and finding
the best fit for this role is our top priority — that’s why our process is
longer than usual. At every stage, we try to be respectful of your time
and grateful you’re spending it with us.

• Application and eligibility check — work authorization, timezone, availability

•
Async assessment — 12 scenario-based, multiple-choice questions
(~30 min) + when qualifying; 3 open questions (max. 45 min)

• If you pass the multiple choice section, you will be asked to complete 3 open written questions (max. 45 min)

• Portfolio review — the design team will review your best work and thinking

• Behavioral interview — a conversation with our People team about how you work

• Take-home design task — ~60 minutes, scoped for this role, AI tools encouraged

• Hiring team interview — with a design team member and the Head of UX

• Skip-level conversation — with executive leadership

• Reference checks

We give honest, timely feedback at every step. Job searches are hard; we
don't want to make yours harder.

Compensation and setup

The pay range for this role is €60,000 - 90,000. Miaplaza’s compensation
philosophy ensures equity and competitiveness while considering regional
differences in labor costs. Placement within a range is determined based
on factors such as demonstrated skills, internal equity, and local labor
market rates for the candidate’s geographic area.

opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. If you

Our North Star is to take the friction out of bringing digital ideas to life, making room for your ideas and productivity.

Developers from some of the biggest companies in the world are using WunderGraph to design and streamline their API environments. We raised our Series A ($7.5 million USD) in March 2025, being backed by eBay, Karma Ventures, and Aspenwood Ventures.

The culture we are creating together is extremely important to us. Read here how we are Building the Company We Always Wanted to Work In .

We invite everyone that wants to join us to understand our Core Beliefs and if you want to make an impact, have your voice heard, and work in a no-BS organization where you can get stuff done, look no further and apply today so we can chat.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Product Designer at WunderGraph, you are the connection between what our users will find most helpful and what our engineers build. Considering the users also happen to be other developers, this becomes an interesting challenge to think about the Developer Experience as the User Experience. You combine sharp user insight, craft, and pragmatism to deliver experiences that are elegant, usable, and built to scale.

This is a wide-reaching role, as design roles at a startup should be. One week you might be running user interviews to shape a new feature; the next, refining our design system or designing a marketing landing page. You ground your work in evidence rather than assumption, partner closely with product and engineering, and turn what you learn about users into a clear, informed UX strategy that guides where we go next.

TEAM INTEGRATION

•
Reports to the VP of Product; is part of the Product team

•
Aligns closely with the CEO (Product) and Head of Customer Success (customer experience and business impact)

•
Collaborate within the Product team with the Delivery Lead and the Design Engineer

•
Collaborates cross-functionally with engineering, marketing, product, and customer success

ROLE OBJECTIVES

You are successful if you:

•
Take ownership of the complete design lifecycle, bridging the gap between initial discovery and final delivery for web and product interfaces.

•
Cultivate an evidence-based UX strategy that leverages user research and data to steer the product's evolution.

•
Oversee the growth of a unified and extensible design system that spans both our product and marketing efforts.

•
Convert user insights and organizational objectives into pragmatic, human-centric solutions engineered for long-term scalability.

•
Advocate for excellence in accessibility, responsiveness, and performance as fundamental pillars of your craft.

•
Provide mentorship to the team, sharing expertise in research methodologies and design principles.

•
Refine the visual and functional identity of WunderGraph through meticulous and high-impact design work.

•
Impact high-level product strategy by demonstrating how user-focused decisions drive tangible business impact.

ROLE TASKS

The role focuses on, but is not limited to:

Product Design

•
Design and prototype user flows, interfaces, and interactions with scalability in mind.

•
Own design problems end to end. From initial concept through execution and iteration after launch.

•
Rapidly produce wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity designs, exploring multiple concepts and iterating quickly.

•
Define and evolve our design system and component library, keeping it consistent and maintainable.

•
Partner closely with engineers on feasibility, quality, and handoff, contributing to technical decisions (and coding where you're comfortable and it helps as a plus, not a requirement).

•
Introduce advanced prototyping, interaction design, and motion practices.

UX Research & Strategy

•
Plan and conduct user research across discovery and validation via user interviews, surveys, usability testing, and competitor analysis.

•
Turn ambiguous product questions into decision-grade research that maps to real product and design decisions.

•
Synthesize findings into clear insights, personas, journey maps, and opportunity areas that the team can act on.

•
Build and maintain a shared insight repository so learning is reusable, searchable, and available to everyone.

•
Translate research into an informed, evolving UX strategy that guides the roadmap and anchors design direction in real user needs.

•
Advocate for the user in prioritization and roadmap discussions, and define what "better" looks like through clear UX success metrics.

•
Run discovery workshops and share insights so research shows up where decisions are made like in design reviews, product planning, and standups embedding user knowledge from the get-go.

Web & Brand Experience

•
Own the design and evolution of WunderGraph's web presence.

•
Deliver assets that span product and marketing: landing pages, visuals, campaign graphics, and interactive components.

•
Shape and maintain a cohesive style guide, balancing design innovation with consistency.

•
Support brand storytelling with motion graphics and interactive elements.

ROLE REQUIREMENTS

•
Senior-level experience in Product Design or UX/UI Design, with a strong portfolio of shipped work.

•
Proven experience planning and running UX research (both generative and evaluative) and turning findings into strategy.

•
Proficiency in Figma, prototyping tools, and Adobe Creative Suite.

•
Strong background in UX and interaction design, accessibility, responsive design, and usability.

•
Experience contributing to or leading design systems and component libraries.

•
Comfortable using data and research to inform and defend design decisions.

•
Working knowledge of front-end technologies (HTML/CSS, JavaScript a plus) enough to collaborate closely with engineers.

•
Excellent communication, storytelling, and collaboration skills in English.

•
A self-starter who is comfortable with ambiguity and can lead initiatives independently in a fast-moving startup.

•
Comfortable working 100% remotely in a distributed team.

•
Willingness to travel occasionally for team retreats and workshops.

Why WunderGraph?

•
Work from wherever you thrive—we’re fully remote and globally distributed. If you're in Miami, come work with us in person! We also provide co-working space options worldwide if needed.

•
Pick your preferred work hardware

•
We focus on getting stuff done, and on having fun whilst doing so: work hard, play hard!

•
You can make a real difference and find lots of opportunities to grow together with us

•
Discretionary PTO: take the time you need to recharge

•
Competitive compensation

•
Depending on location, we offer healthcare benefits according to local standards

•
Team retreats across the globe

Note: This is a full-time, fully remote position. We are looking for someone who is available to work during European (CET) business hours.

The Process

We respect your time and interest in WunderGraph. This is why we're aiming to make the process as fast as possible. Here's what you can expect:

•
30 min intro call with Mariya from our People team

•
45 min discussion with the hiring manager. Following this, you might receive a small take home assignment related to the role. This is your chance to prove your skill!

Complete the assignment and review together with hiring manager

•
Meet the founders

•
Culture fit call with team members

•
Offer

Our process also includes reference and background checks. We aim to respond or provide feedback in 2 or 3 days between each stage of the process. We're usually hiring through Deel as our Employer of Record, except for Germany or Florida where we're hiring directly.

Design at Remote

Our strategic and user-centered designers start with customer insights and envision how people experience Remote’s products. What you bring

• An IC product designer who is very experienced, and whose work history and portfolio demonstrates that they have clearly mastered the key pillars of their end-to-end craft.

• Preference will be given to candidates who have experience designing complex solutions for complete digital environments. Deep Fintech, HR tech, B2B or SaaS experience is a plus for this position.

• Work history that demonstrates your ability to autonomously own design for your team or feature area.

• An impressive portfolio of work that shows how your design work consistently delivers outstanding results for both the business and for end users.

• Work that demonstrates your experience and product design craft via simplicity, typography, interaction design and UI design.

• Case studies that help us understand your full end-to-end design process from insight gathering through to defining the customer problem, conceptual design, delivery, measurement and optimization.

• Clear evidence that you are an effective cross-functional collaborator within your dev team who uses feedback, consensus building and conflict resolution to drive great outcomes.

• Persuasive communication that helps you confidently build narratives around your design work to bring your team along with you - with, clear, fluent written and spoken English that will help you communicate effectively with colleagues all over the world.

• Evidence that you are beginning to have a wider influence on your design team - you may mentor others and share work that has an impact on the larger design team.

• Candidates that embody and demonstrate our core values at Remote.
