Stability AI is the leader in purpose-built AI products for professional creatives across music, gaming, and entertainment.

Stability AI sparked the generative AI revolution when it announced the release of Stable Diffusion in August 2022, putting generative technology in the hands of millions of creators globally and cementing its position as a leader in the field. Stable Diffusion models have since been downloaded more than 350 million times, serving as the technical foundation for an entire ecosystem of work.

We build for creatives first. Our work expands beyond the models themselves into products and solutions designed for specific production workflows. This artist-centric approach is why Electronic Arts, Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, WPP, and others have chosen us as their strategic partner.

Stability AI is recognized among Fortune's 50 AI Innovators and TIME's Most Influential Companies, with Stable Audio named to TIME's Best Inventions list. In June 2024, Stability AI entered a new phase of growth with a leadership team including CEO Prem Akkaraju, Executive Chairman Sean Parker, and Board Member James Cameron, alongside board members Dana Settle and Thomas Laffont.

The company is backed by world-class investors including interactive entertainment innovator Electronic Arts; global leaders in music entertainment Sony Music Group, Universal Music Group, and Warner Music Group; investment firms Greycroft, Coatue, WPP, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sound Ventures, AMD Ventures, and Mantis Capital; and individual investors Sean Parker, Eric Schmidt, and James Cameron.

You can learn more at stability.ai .

Stability AI is unlocking the power of open-source generative AI to expand human creativity. We build world-class models that are accessible, adaptable, and designed to empower creators, developers, and enterprises everywhere.

Flint is hiring a

Remote Product Designer

Compensation: $160k–190k base + meaningful equity

About Flint

The best education anyone has ever received is one person paying close attention to one student: moving at their pace, noticing what they missed, asking the next question at the right moment. But the current system is built around a compromise with one teacher managing thirty students.

Flint exists to take that compromise off the table. Personalized learning, at the scale of a whole school — every student working with something closer to a tutor, and every teacher able to see what's actually happening across their class instead of guessing.

Go look at the product before you read any further: app.flintk12.com

The Role

Students want something that stays with them, going at their pace and helps them get unstuck without just handing over the answer. Teachers want that happening inside a class they still control, and they'd like their evenings back. Admins want proof that the platform they rolled out is leading to teacher productivity and student progress.

Your job is to dive deep into this design problem, holding three sets of needs within one product. We’ll trust you to ship designs that are the best possible solution to our users most urgent pain points. tl;dr you'll get to own how Flint works and how it feels.

How We Work

• We move fast, and closely. You'll work with a small, senior team: one Product Lead, a Chief of Staff (Product), a CTO, and five engineers. We also have a running joke that we can’t keep up with our #product_updates channel because of how much we ship.

• Fast and good aren't in tension here. In our experience the fastest route to something good is getting a rough version in front of a real teacher early, which tends to be quicker than getting it right in private. Decisions with the highest impact have often happened within days, not month long sprints.

• We’re always learning. Call it on-brand or a bit on the nose, but learning from each other, our customers, the market have been key to our growth. We even have channels dedicated to sharing our workflow mistakes and wins. Education is also still being actively shaped as a field, and staying tuned to what users and the industry are telling us matters more than assuming we already know.

• Users drive our decisions. Our team isn't exclusively made up of former teachers, and that's deliberate. We'd rather build from real user feedback and a range of perspectives than from any one person's classroom experience. Our close connection with teachers, students, and admins helps us quickly understand what's working and what isn't.

• We design with AI, not around it. Lo-fi concepts out of Claude, prototypes we can put in front of a teacher the same week, PRDs drafted from screenshots and voice notes: these are just a few ways we’ve used AI to support our work, and it's a real part of why our loop is as short as it is.

What You'll Do

• Dig deep, validate, and design. Validate the user goals, map key journeys, and land on the actual jobs to be done. People will hand you solutions along the way: the useful move is usually to find the need underneath before taking the solution at face value.

• Explore broadly, then narrow. Iteration is key. For a complex UI, we'd expect five or six real concepts on the table before committing to one, whether it sketches, wireframes, AI-generated lo-fi, competitor and industry research…whatever gets you there fastest. Then you cut it down with your own judgment, a review with someone on the team, and wherever we can manage it, real users.

• Design zero to one, and one to a hundred. Some of this is a genuinely new problem where you shape the whole thing from scratch. Some of it is taking something we shipped early and making it scalable, coherent, and delightful in the way the first version never had time to be.

• Communicate your judgment effectively. You can clearly explain the context, intent, designs, and the reasoning behind your work to the rest of the team.

• Set the design bar. Our design system and design philosophy are still taking form. You'll decide what becomes a pattern, what stays a one-off, and where the whole thing goes from here.

• Stay through QA and impact. You'll have a say in what gets QA'd and in what metrics tell us whether the thing actually worked. Shipping isn't the end of your involvement.

• Impact hundreds of thousands of learners. How a generation learns to think alongside AI is being decided right now, in the products that get built this year. Very few designers get to work on something this consequential this early.

What We're Looking For

• You've designed and shipped real software. We care far more about one thing you made and can talk us through than about ten polished case-study slides.

• You can run the whole arc, from understanding the problem through concepts, hi-fi, and a spec engineering can build from. Not every step has to be your strongest.

• You're comfortable with being scrappy and being iterative. You'd rather put a rough thing in front of a real teacher than a perfect thing in front of your own team.

• You want to shape a category-defining product. You're excited by building something that hasn't existed before and genuinely changes how people learn — not iterating on the margins of something that already works.

• You're here to learn, not just to apply what you already know. That means sharpening your design skills and process on the job, and getting deep on the education industry itself, from US private K–12 to foreign education ministries and everything in between. You find that range interesting rather than intimidating.

• You care about education. You should like what you are building and who you are building for!

What We Offer

• Meaningful equity.

• Health and dental insurance.

• Personal device stipend.

About us:

BetterMe — an all-in-one well-being ecosystem empowering millions to become better — physically, mentally, and emotionally. We build what makes people better and keep challenging ourselves to inspire others.

As a Product Designer at BetterMe, you will create visually engaging B2C experiences that combine strong graphic design with product thinking. You will work on funnels, landing pages, and other user journeys, exploring creative concepts and using AI tools to turn product and marketing ideas into polished designs that drive user engagement and business results.

Your impact:

• Design and improve B2C user experiences, quizzes, funnels, landing pages, and other product flows.

• Create visually strong concepts that communicate the right message and support product and marketing goals.

• Explore multiple design directions and propose creative solutions rather than stopping at the first idea.

• Work closely with Product, Development, QA, and other designers to bring ideas from concept to production.

• Collaborate with product teams on experiments, iterations, and improvements based on business priorities.

• Use AI tools in your daily design workflow, including image generation and tools such as Claude.

• Create and adapt visual assets while keeping them relevant to the product, audience, and context.

• Prepare clear design specifications and ensure high-quality implementation together with developers.

• Contribute ideas and hypotheses based on your understanding of users, the product, and business goals.

About you:

• A strong portfolio demonstrating excellent visual and graphic design skills — this is one of the key things we’ll be looking at.

• Experience designing B2C digital products, marketing-driven experiences, quizzes, funnels, landing pages, or similar user journeys.

• Experience with A/B testing and designing for experimentation.

• Strong command of typography, composition, imagery, and visual storytelling.

• Product mindset: you understand that design is not only about aesthetics, but also about user behavior, conversion, and business outcomes.

• Ability to work quickly, iterate, and adapt when product or business priorities change.

• Proactive and independent approach: you can work with an open-ended task, explore alternatives, and make decisions without requiring detailed instructions at every step.

• Ability to present and explain your design decisions and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

• Experience using AI tools for design and image generation, or strong motivation to actively incorporate them into your workflow.

• Curiosity, ownership, and willingness to continuously learn and experiment.

Will be a plus:

• Hands-on experience designing quizzes or conversion-focused funnels.

• Previous experience in a creative/digital agency, especially working on campaigns, promotional websites, social media creatives, or other visually driven projects.

• Experience working in a fast-paced B2C product company.

• Experience using AI not only for content and image generation, but also for improving or automating parts of your design workflow.

What you get at BetterMe:

A mission that matters. Every product, design, and idea we create helps millions of people become healthier and more confident.
Trust without micromanagement. You’ll have the autonomy to manage your time, make decisions, and take ownership of your work. We value outcomes, not hours online.
Room to grow. 90% of our leads have grown within the company. You’ll have space to take initiative, expand your responsibilities, and develop your career
Wellness in practice.
Offline: workouts with professional trainers in our corporate gym, massage, corporate lunches, sports activities, and team events.
Online: regular online workouts, partner discounts, and free access to BetterMe products.
Medical insurance and access to a corporate doctor.
Vacation and work-life balance. 20 paid vacation days, paid sick leave, and additional days off around public holidays.
Open communication. Transparency between teams, direct feedback, and support for new ideas are part of how we work.
Support for sports activities. We cover participation fees for sporting events and encourage our team to take part together.
Modern equipment. We provide up-to-date hardware and everything you need to work effectively.
Legal and financial support. Our experienced legal and finance teams are available to help with work-related documentation and consultations.

Find more about us on social media platforms: Instagram , LinkedIn .

Mission

To advance the adoption of the Walrus Protocol – a Verifiable Data Platform for AI Builders

Vision

To create a foundation for AI builders to store and manage their data, making that data persistent, portable, and under their control across apps, providers, and agents.

Walrus Foundation is looking for a Staff Product Designer to define and own the product experience for Walrus.

Walrus is infrastructure for developers, and designing infrastructure products requires a particular kind of product thinking. Users need to navigate technical concepts, understand system state, work with large amounts of information, configure resources, diagnose problems, and take actions that can have real consequences for their data, storage, or spend.

You’ll partner closely with product and engineering from the earliest stages of discovery through implementation. You won’t receive finished requirements and turn them into screens. You’ll help determine which problems matter, investigate how developers actually work, challenge assumptions, prototype and test potential solutions, and ultimately define how developers experience Walrus.

As a Staff designer, you’ll also establish the systems and standards that allow the product to scale. You’ll think beyond individual features to create consistent interaction patterns, reusable components, and product principles that make the entire Walrus experience more coherent over time.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

– Own the Walrus product experience. Define and evolve the end-to-end developer experience across Walrus’s product surfaces and key workflows.

– Lead discovery with product and engineering. Help frame problems before the team jumps to solutions, identify unanswered questions, and determine what evidence we need before committing to build.

– Bring developers directly into the design process. Conduct lightweight developer interviews and usability tests, put prototypes in front of real users, and synthesize findings into decisions the team can act on.

– Design complex technical workflows. Create flows, wireframes, prototypes, and production-ready designs for experiences involving dense data, system state, configuration, resource management, and high-consequence actions.

– Influence product direction. Bring a strong point of view on what Walrus should build—not just how features should look—and constructively challenge product and engineering assumptions when needed.

– Build Walrus’s design system. Establish and maintain shared components, interaction patterns, and product principles that create consistency and allow the product surface to grow without fragmenting.

– Benchmark the market. Regularly tear down comparable developer and infrastructure products to understand established patterns, identify opportunities, and avoid reinventing solved problems.

– Stay close through implementation. Partner with engineering throughout development, review what ships against the intended experience, catch problems early, and incorporate requirements and feedback from partners such as Legal.

– Raise the design bar. Establish what excellent developer-product design looks like for Walrus and help create the practices that maintain that standard as the organization grows.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

– 8-10 years of product design experience, with demonstrated ownership of complex technical products.

– A portfolio demonstrating ownership of shipped developer tools, cloud/infrastructure products, consoles, dashboards, or similarly complex technical products.

– Demonstrated ability to simplify technically sophisticated workflows without removing the control or information expert users need.

– Strong interaction-design skills across data-heavy interfaces, tables, configuration, complex states, progressive disclosure, permissions, errors, and high-consequence actions.

– Experience independently identifying and framing product problems rather than primarily executing against predefined requirements.

– A track record of influencing product strategy and roadmap decisions through design.

– Strong qualitative research instincts and experience incorporating lightweight user research and usability testing into day-to-day product work.

– Experience creating or significantly evolving design systems and reusable interaction patterns.

– Strong partnership with engineering and a willingness to remain involved through implementation and design QA.

– Excellent communication skills and the confidence to disagree constructively with senior product and engineering partners.

– Comfort operating with significant autonomy in an ambiguous, rapidly evolving technical environment.

We’re actively expanding our reach across key EU markets like Germany, France, the Netherlands, Italy, and Spain.

At Finom, we’re not just redefining the entrepreneurial experience — we’re empowering our employees to make a real difference. Your work matters, and your impact extends far beyond product metrics. We nurture innovation and an inspiring work environment where bold ideas thrive, prioritizing thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and our business as a whole.

Maintaining our start-up spirit, we prioritize thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and, of course, our business.

As a Senior Product Designer, you will be a key contributor and owner within one of Finom’s core product domains, driving end-to-end design for features that directly shape the financial lives of tens of thousands of customers.

What You’ll Do

• Own design delivery across the full product lifecycle , from discovery and conceptualization to final implementation and polish.

• Translate complex business and user problems into clear, user-centered design solutions.

• Collaborate closely with product managers and engineers to effectively scope, prioritize, and define project outcomes.

• Create essential design artifacts including user flows, wireframes, high-fidelity mockups, and interactive prototypes.

• Contribute actively to our design system and maintain consistency and scalability across the entire user interface.

• Participate robustly in usability testing, user feedback loops, and data-driven experimentation.

• Support high-priority initiatives such as modular pricing, onboarding UX transformation, and the development of AI Copilot features.

Who You Are

• 4+ years of experience in product design , ideally gained within fast-paced fintech or SaaS environments.

• A strong portfolio that clearly demonstrates user-centered thinking and polished execution across various projects.

• Experience working on complex platforms with multiple user flows, states, and feature dependencies.

• Confidence working in cross-functional squads with engineers, analysts, and product managers.

• The ability to rationalize your design decisions rigorously using data, research insights, and direct customer feedback.

• A strong foundation of curiosity, pragmatism, and a consistently high bar for design quality and craft.

Nice to Have

Work & Swim program

Summary of the Role:

As a Product Designer at Maze, you’ll define what product design looks like for AI agents in cybersecurity — a problem space where the design patterns don’t exist yet. This is an early-hire role at a well-funded Series A startup building at the intersection of generative AI and security, and you’ll own the product surface end-to-end while working directly with our Head of Product, engineering, and founders.

The product challenge is genuinely new. Our AI agents investigate vulnerabilities autonomously, surface findings with real context, and collaborate with security teams to cut through noise. Your job is to design how humans and agents work together — how trust gets built, how decisions get communicated, how complex security workflows become understandable. There’s no playbook for this. You’ll create one.

This role suits someone who operates closer to a product director than a screen-shipper — driving direction, influencing strategy, and making business-impact calls, alongside the visual craft to deliver them. You’ll be using AI tools daily to move faster, but your craft is the floor: every design choice should hold up on its own merits, independent of how it was generated. Success looks like a design system shipped and adopted across the product, and concrete product outcomes — feature adoption, POC-to-customer conversion, and customer satisfaction with the experiences you ship.

Your Contribution:

•

Define AI-Agent UX Patterns: Design how security teams collaborate with autonomous AI agents — how investigations get presented, how trust is established, how humans steer the agent without slowing it down. You’re inventing patterns, not applying existing ones.

•

Drive Product Direction, Not Just Design: Operate as a product-led designer — shaping roadmap, challenging requirements, influencing leadership with research and business reasoning. The bar is “what should we build, and why” alongside “how should it look.”

•

Own the Product Surface End-to-End: Take features from problem framing through shipped product, working in tight partnership with PMs and engineers — including backend. Run discovery, prototype rapidly, validate with customers, and stay close to implementation. No throwing designs over the wall, no shipping around the engineering team.

•

Build the Design System: Create and scale a component-based design system that becomes the foundation for everything we ship. Establish patterns for AI-human collaboration that the team can build on as we grow.

•

Pioneer AI-Assisted Design Workflows: Use AI tools to accelerate ideation, prototyping, and exploration — and develop the methodologies the rest of the team will adopt. Your daily workflow is itself a contribution.

•

Translate Research Into Design: Run customer research, talk to security teams directly, and turn what you learn into shipped product. Use AI-assisted analysis to move from insight to prototype in days, not weeks.

•

Set the Quality Bar: Establish what “good” looks like for product design at Maze across craft, consistency, and customer impact — as the foundation for a design team that scales behind you.

What You Need to Be Successful:

•

Visual Craft for Data-Dense UI: A portfolio that holds up to detailed scrutiny — strong colour theory, deliberate visual hierarchy, considered information architecture for complex workflows. This is the bar, not a nice-to-have. Your interview will dig into specific design choices and why you made them.

•

Product Design Track Record: 4-7 years of professional product design experience, with shipped work in B2B SaaS. We’re flexible on years; demonstrated craft and clear ownership matter more than time served.

•

Data-Heavy B2B Interfaces: Direct experience designing for complex workflows, dense data, and technical audiences. Dashboards, investigation tools, developer products, security platforms — the kind of UI where information density and decision support actually matter.

•

AI as Tool, Not Crutch: You use AI tools (Figma AI, Cursor, v0, Midjourney, ChatGPT/Claude, etc.) as part of your daily workflow and can speak credibly to what they’re good for and where they break down. Critically, every design choice you ship should hold up on its own — AI accelerates your work, it doesn’t substitute for foundational craft.

•

Product-Strategic Thinking: Track record of driving product direction, not just executing on briefs. You’ve influenced what to build with research, framed problems for leadership, and made business-impact calls — ideally in environments where you operated without a dedicated PM.

•

Deep Engineering Collaboration: Demonstrable history of shipping work in tight partnership with engineers — including backend. Pairing on implementation, working in design tokens, understanding the systems your designs land in, building consensus rather than shipping around resistance.

•

Design Systems Experience: Background building or meaningfully contributing to a design system in a production product. You think in components, tokens, and patterns, not one-off screens.

•

Customer-Led Approach: Comfortable running discovery directly with users, synthesising what you hear, and using that to make calls about what to build. You don’t wait for research to be handed to you.

•

Nice to haves:

•

Experience designing for cybersecurity, developer tools, or other technical product domains

•

Background designing agentic or AI-native product experiences (not just AI features bolted onto existing products)

•

Early-stage startup experience where you’ve operated without a manager or established design function

Why Join Us:

•

Define a New Design Space: AI agents in security is a genuinely new problem. The interaction patterns, trust models, and workflows don’t exist yet — you’ll create them. The work you do here will influence how this entire category gets designed.

•

Fast-Track to Design Leadership: This is a founding-trajectory role and we’re hiring for someone who wants a long-term home, not a stepping stone. As the team scales, the natural path is IC → Lead → Head of Design. If you have leadership ambitions, you’ll have the runway to grow into them. If you’d rather stay deeply hands-on, the IC scope grows with the product.

•

Ambitious Challenge: We’re using generative AI (LLMs and agents) to solve one of the most pressing problems in cybersecurity — the gap between vulnerability findings and meaningful action. You’ll be designing at the cutting edge of this field.

•

Expert Team: Work alongside hands-on leaders with experience in Big Tech and Scale-ups. Our team has been part of the leadership teams behind multiple acquisitions and an IPO.

•

Impactful Work: Cybersecurity is a force for good. The experiences you design will directly affect how security teams protect organisations worldwide.

•

Build an AI-Native Company: We’re building a new company in the AI era with the opportunity to design everything from the ground up — including how the design function itself works. You’ll help pioneer AI-assisted design practices and set new standards.

You will be FORT’s first full-time designer, responsible for building the design platform from 0→1 across hardware interaction, operator-facing software, and AI-assisted workflows. This role spans all three product pillars: Control, Intelligence, and Ecosystem. You will not be decorating screens; you will define how people interact with our hardware, software, and the autonomous systems that run on both.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Build FORT’s design foundation from scratch: design system, interaction model, and component library across FORT Manager and future platform surfaces.
- Design the physical interaction layer of FORT hardware, how operators read device state, safety status, and control affordances through button layout, LED signaling, and tactile feedback.
- Define human-robot interaction (HRI) patterns: how operators monitor, trust, intervene in, and recover autonomous systems, across both hardware and software surfaces.
- Design AI-forward workflows: AI Assistant interface, fleet observability dashboards, anomaly surfacing, and operator guidance experiences. Use AI tools actively to prototype and iterate faster.
- Conduct field research with industrial operators and OEM engineers in real deployment environments; run usability testing and translate findings directly into design decisions.
- Map end-to-end platform journeys across all user types: floor operators, OEM integration engineers, fleet administrators, and safety stakeholders.
- Partner daily with Product, Firmware, Software, Hardware, and Operations; translate technical constraints into design decisions without sacrificing usability.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

- 5+ years of product or interaction design experience, including at least 2 years in hardware-software combined environments, robotics, IoT, industrial automation, automotive, or similar.
- Built a design system or component library from scratch, not inherited one.
- Physical interaction design experience: designed how a hardware product communicates state, intent, or safety status to a human.
- Field research experience: contextual inquiry, operator shadowing, or usability testing in real-world environments.
- Proficient in Figma or equivalent, Claude; prototypes complex, multi-step workflows at high fidelity.
- AI-first approach: uses AI tools to accelerate design, prototyping, and research synthesis as a standard workflow, not a novelty.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

- Experience in safety-critical or regulated product environments (human factors, IEC 62366, or equivalent).
- Background in human-robot interaction, autonomous systems, or physical AI platforms.
- Familiarity with front-end basics (HTML/CSS) for tighter design-engineering handoff.

Speel is an AI-powered video creation platform. Users upload a product image or URL, and the AI generates UGC-style video ads — unboxing sequences, talking-head reviews, product demos — without manual editing or production teams.
Our primary users are content agencies producing ad creatives at scale, but we're building for any creator. Think of the Figma model: built for professional teams, loved by individuals.
We're looking for a product/UI designer to own the interface end-to-end.

**Our design philosophy**
We want to be Apple, not Samsung. That means: fewer controls exposed, smarter defaults, opinionated choices that reduce decision fatigue, and a premium feel that signals quality before the user generates anything. The interface should feel like a tool built by someone who deeply understands the creator's workflow — not a wrapper around AI APIs.
We care about: fast time-to-value (the user knows what to do within seconds), clarity over cleverness, reducing cognitive load without removing capability, and visual quality that builds trust.

**What you'll design**

- A mode-based creative workspace — A single-screen interface with a top navigation bar (mode tabs), a left sidebar (model selection, settings, input configuration), a center gallery grid (generated media), and a sticky bottom bar (AI copilot chat, status, and controls). One screen, many states.
- AI copilot interaction patterns — A chat-based copilot that orchestrates the workspace in real-time. You'll design how the AI communicates what it's doing, how it asks for user decisions (multiple-choice approval flows), and how multi-step generation workflows feel as they execute progressively.
- Sub-mode selection and discovery — A modal system for browsing curated presets across AI models — each with preview thumbnails, model names, and descriptions. This needs to scale as models and presets grow without becoming overwhelming.
- Dynamic, context-aware UI — Settings, input slots, gallery actions, and available tools change based on the active mode and model. The interface must feel stable and clear even as its contents shift dynamically.
- State-rich design — Gallery empty vs. populating vs. full. AI generating vs. idle. Modal open vs. closed. Copilot asking an MCQ vs. streaming status. You'll think through every meaningful state, not just the happy path.

**What we're looking for**

- Taste above all. Typography, color, spacing, and composition that feel intentional across every element. Nothing looks generic or pulled from a component library. Your portfolio should make us stop scrolling.
- Fast UX comprehension. You can look at an unfamiliar product, absorb the interaction logic quickly, and improve it — without needing everything explained to you.
- Empathic design thinking. You put yourself in the shoes of a creator who just wants to make a video, not learn a new tool. Your decisions reflect user mindset, not just aesthetic preference.
- Figma fluency. Clean, well-structured files that engineers can ship from. Named layers, organized pages, logical component usage.
- Comfort with complexity. You've designed tools people spend hours in — not just landing pages or simple CRUD apps. Mode-based interfaces, dynamic settings panels, real-time feedback patterns.

**Nice to have**

- Experience designing creative tools, media/video platforms, or studio-style workspaces.
- Familiarity with AI-powered product patterns — prompt interfaces, generation feedback, copilot UX.
- You admire the design quality of products like Runway, Linear, Arc, or Rive — and can articulate why.

**Details**

- Role type: Full-time
- Compensation: Competitive salary
- Stage: Early — you'll define the product's visual identity and interaction language from scratch

Zed is building a new kind of programming environment.

We’re not just designing a code editor. We’re designing the environment where humans and AI build software together.

Zed combines high-performance local editing, real-time collaboration, and AI agents that can work directly in the codebase.

We’re looking for a Product Design Engineer to help shape how this environment works.

Designers at Zed work closely with engineers, prototype ideas directly in the product, and often implement parts of the interface themselves.

## What you'll work on

The editor sits at the center of how developers read, understand, and evolve complex systems. Small interaction decisions can meaningfully shape that process.

You might work on:

- Collaborative programming workflows
- Interaction models for AI agents that read and modify code
- Navigating and understanding large codebases
- Keyboard-driven workflows and command systems
- Interfaces for Git, debugging, and code exploration
- Zed’s design system and interaction patterns
- Prototyping and implementing UI in the product

Many of the interaction patterns we’re exploring don’t yet have established precedents.

## How you'll work

Design is tightly integrated with engineering.

Designers often pair with engineers, exploring ideas directly in the product. Many interactions start as small experiments in the codebase rather than static mockups.

We care deeply about clarity, performance, simplicity, and craft.

## What we're looking for

You might be a good fit if you:

- Have strong product design experience
- Care deeply about interaction design
- Enjoy working on technical products
- Prototype ideas in code
- You enjoy operating on the bleeding edge, work well with ambiguity, and ship
- You are excited to learn some Rust and get your hands dirty creating interfaces in [Zed's custom-built UI framework, GPUI](https://www.gpui.rs/)

- Developer tools or IDEs
- Code editors or programming environments
- Technical productivity software
- AI-assisted tools or developer platforms
- Complex productivity products

Zed is multiplayer by default, allowing developers to work together in the same codebase in real time. Much of our work happens through pair programming, with engineers collaborating directly inside the editor.

We ship improvements weekly and work closely with a community that cares deeply about the craft of developer tools.

Join us in revolutionizing the development experience. Your expertise could drive Zed's next game-changing feature!

About Casper Studios
We’re an AI services firm that helps companies figure out where and how to use AI. We’ve bootstrapped Casper Studios to roughly 40 people, worked with 30+ clients, and done deals with some of the largest companies, PE funds, and model providers.

The reason comes down to how we work with clients. Before we build anything, we listen, understand the business, and help them figure out the highest-leverage way to get started on their AI journey.

About the Role
We are hiring a UX/UI Designer who can plug into live build teams and move quickly. This position will take rough requirements and turn them into a clean, buildable interface within a short timeline. There will rarely be a perfect brief and a long runway. This role sits right next to engineers, owns the UX/UI surface end to end, and raises the bar on how our work looks and feels.

The engagement will begin as a flexible structure and can grow into something bigger as the work grows and we find fit. If this sounds good to you, we would love for you to apply.

What You’ll Do
•
Design and ship the UI/UX for AI products we build with clients, from core app flows to brand-new features

•
Work shoulder to shoulder with engineers in fast build cycles, turning rough requirements into usable product quickly

•
Own the full surface: information architecture, interaction design, and high-fidelity UI in Figma

•
Design for AI-native experiences, reading and review views, agent interactions, chat versus structured surfaces, and the states that come with probabilistic output

•
Jump across multiple product builds at once and keep quality high without slowing the team down

•
Translate messy stakeholder input into clear, shippable design, and know when to push back on scope

•
Establish lightweight design patterns and a reusable system so we stop redrawing the same things across projects

•
Own end-to-end user flows and information architecture for complex, data-dense products

•
Decide what to surface and what to hold back, apply progressive disclosure so users aren't buried under information-heavy AI output

What You’ll Bring
•
A strong design portfolio, with real shipped software, not just concept work

•
Fluency in Figma and modern UI craft; you can go from wireframe to polished, buildable UI fast

•
Comfort designing for AI products and for requirements that shift as the product gets real

•
Ability to work directly with engineers and make pragmatic tradeoffs to get things shipped

•
Strong judgment on when something needs to be pixel-perfect and when it just needs to move

•
High agency, low ego, fast, and reliable under deadline, people trust you to run with things

•
Daily usage of AI tools in your design workflow

Nice To Haves
•
Experience building or maintaining a design system

Range across multiple verticals such as finance, healthcare, or customer experience

Experience in HR tech (or a similarly complex, workflow-heavy B2B domain)

Senior UI/UX Designer

Employment Type: Full-Time, Experienced

Department: Information Technology

CGS is seeking a Senior UI/UX Designer to join our team supporting a wide-ranging technical support initiative for a large Federal agency.

CGS brings motivated, highly skilled, and creative people together to solve the government’s most dynamic problems with cutting-edge technology. To carry out our mission, we are seeking candidates who are excited to contribute to government innovation, appreciate collaboration, and can anticipate the needs of others. Here at CGS, we offer an environment in which our employees feel supported, and we encourage professional growth through various learning opportunities.

Skills and attributes for success:

-Lead full-scale UX design efforts to include research, blueprinting, and evaluating existing systems.

-Manage the planning, design, and implementation of multiple sites and applications across multiple clients simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.

-Lead all phases of user research and analysis needed to inform the creation of highly usable web pages, application interfaces, and other dynamic solutions.

-Collaborate with federal practice engineers and federal clients to define, design, and implement innovative, beautiful, intuitive solutions for use by our federal customer and their stakeholders.

-Create wireframes, storyboards, and site maps to effectively communicate interaction and design ideas for websites and applications.

-Create scalable design resources to aid in project collaboration and the expansion of ECS creative services.

Qualifications:

-Bachelor's Degree.

-Must be able to obtain a Public Trust.

-Strong UX design experience.

-10+ years combined professional design experience (UCD, UI/UX design).

-Strong online portfolio that showcases the candidate’s ability to make research-driven decisions in the design of responsive web and mobile applications.

-Results-oriented problem solver with high standards for quality, accuracy, attention to detail, and overall excellence.

-Expertise in user research methodologies, user centered design principles and frameworks, and user interface design standards.

-Advanced understanding of user personas, user flows, affinity mapping, and other research tools.

-Strong understanding of the life cycle process of website development (discovery, planning, design, requirements, coding, testing, and user testing and evaluation).

-Experience evaluating existing systems and processes to identify UX issues and develop UX recommendations.

-Experience designing web and mobile applications that are compliant with 508 and US Web Design System (USWDS) standards.

-Experience prioritizing features while accounting for user goals and business requirements.

-Experience carrying designs from start to finish, from wireframes to delivery of final high-fidelity UI mockups.

-Experience establishing and maintaining rapid customer feedback loops to inform design at critical stages.

-Self-starter, motivated, confident and has ability to work independently as well as in a team environment.

-Success on projects designed from scratch as well as redesigns for established platforms or products.

-Experience mentoring/leading junior designers.

-Advanced coding knowledge (HTML, CSS, and JS).

-Advanced proficiency in Adobe xD, InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop.

Ideally, you will also have:

-Excellent interpersonal and client focused skills— interacts well with all levels of staff and partners with a positive and enthusiastic attitude.

-Experience using Agile methodology to manage projects.

-Experience creating and modifying data visualizations.

-Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite.

Our Commitment:

Contact Government Services (CGS) strives to simplify and enhance government bureaucracy through the optimization of human, technical, and financial resources. We combine cutting-edge technology with world-class personnel to deliver customized solutions that fit our client’s specific needs. We are committed to solving the most challenging and dynamic problems.

For the past seven years, we’ve been growing our government contracting portfolio, and along the way, we’ve created valuable partnerships by demonstrating a commitment to honesty, professionalism, and quality work.

Here at CGS we value honesty through hard work and self-awareness, professionalism in all we do, and to deliver the best quality to our consumers mending those relations for years to come.

We care about our employees. Therefore, we offer a comprehensive benefits package.

-Health, Dental, and Vision

-Life Insurance

-401k

-Flexible Spending Account (Health, Dependent Care, and Commuter)

-Paid Time Off and Observance of State/Federal Holidays

Head of Product Design (UI-Leaning)

Location: Remote, UK-based (London-friendly but not required – occasional in-person meetups, roughly every 4-6 months) Type: Full-time, leadership Salary: Circa £120,000, depending on experience

About the Role

We’re recruiting on behalf of a small, boutique design and development studio with a strong reputation in fintech. Their clients include major global banks and financial institutions, and their core craft is taking complex, legacy financial platforms – trading tools, FX systems, money markets, bond platforms – and completely reinventing the UX, UI, and technical build from the ground up.

They’re deliberately lean: no layers of bureaucracy, no HR department, no room for passengers. Everyone on the team, including leadership, works hands-on in the tools day to day. If you want to lead and keep designing, this is built for you.

The Role

We’re looking for a Head of Product Design to lead their design team and take ownership of how the work looks, feels, and gets delivered to some of the most demanding clients in financial services. This is a backfill for a well-established, senior position with a clear track record behind it – you’ll have real scope to make it your own.

This is not a pure management role. The role splits roughly across:

• Hands-on design – actively working in Figma on live client projects, not just reviewing from a distance.

• Client-facing leadership – presenting design work directly to clients, explaining decisions, and building genuine trust with stakeholders in high-stakes, regulated environments.

• Team oversight – reviewing and sense-checking the work of other designers, keeping projects on track, and helping manage scheduling, often without a dedicated project manager on a given job.

• Quality and brand control – acting as the final check on deliverables, ensuring client branding and design standards are applied consistently.

• Mentoring – supporting the growth and development of the wider design team.

What We’re Looking For

Above all else, we’re looking for someone who fits the ethos of the team: a genuine mentor and leader who brings positive energy day to day, and who can liaise with clients and colleagues with compassion, ease, and confidence. Technical skill matters, but how you show up for people matters just as much.

You’ll ideally bring:

• Strong, current proficiency in Figma, with real experience building and maintaining design systems.

• A track record designing complex, data-heavy interfaces – dashboards, financial platforms, enterprise tools, or similar (not primarily marketing sites or simple consumer apps).

• Confidence and polish presenting to and managing relationships with clients, ideally within a regulated or high-stakes industry.

• Some experience leading, mentoring, or informally managing other designers.

• Comfort working with a high degree of autonomy and ambiguity in a small, low-process team.

Nice to have:

• Direct experience in fintech or financial services.

• Experience taking a legacy product through a full redesign or rebuild.

• Enough development-adjacent fluency to collaborate closely with engineers on technical constraints (no coding required).

We’re not fixed on years of experience – if you can genuinely operate with this level of ownership and client trust, we’d rather hear from you than screen you out on tenure.

Logistics

This role is remote, with a preference for candidates based in or near London. That said, it’s not a hard requirement – we’re open to flexibility for the right person who can comfortably attend team meetups roughly every 4-6 months.

*Rates depend on experience and client requirements

T TROOP is hiring UX Designer

TYPE Full Time CATEGORY UX Design LOCATION Remote EMEA
This job post is over 2 months old and may no longer be available.

Description

UX Designer

Location: Remote based in Spain/South Africa on CET/CAT or similar

TROOP is a group meeting planning and travel management platform that helps companies bring teams together for in-person meetings. The experience starts with TROOP’s award-winning Intelligent Destination Recommendations, which use advanced algorithms to help meeting planners pinpoint the perfect meeting destination, considering travel time, climate impact, budget, lodging availability and safety factors for all attendees.

Using TROOP , companies have saved millions in travel costs, employee time, and carbon emissions, making it possible for people to meet and build stronger relationships with their colleagues, clients, and partners, even in times of tightening budgets and travel restrictions.

Why TROOP?

TROOP believes in the power of shared experiences and the unifying impact of in-person meetings. We are on a mission to bring people together by transforming the meeting planning process.

At TROOP , we have ambitious goals to be the leading provider of end-to-end meeting planning tools. We started by inventing a completely new way for people to decide where to meet, but for us, the destination is just the beginning. We’re developing more innovative solutions that make it easier than ever to organize and host successful group meeting experiences.

TROOP's Culture?

TROOP is an international, remote-first company. Our colleagues are spread across the globe, with entities in Spain, South Africa, the UK, and the United States. Our culture is rooted in an African philosophy called "Ubuntu," which means "I am because we are." It refers to an environment of interdependence through trust. We call ourselves TROOPers, and we are people who seek adventure, challenge the status quo, enjoy innovating, and want to be part of something special. We are doers who roll up our sleeves and get into the details; we own the problem and only stop once it is solved.

We are looking for a UX Designer to design software and platforms. You will combine interfaces and workflows to enhance user experience. In this role, you should be an analytical and creative designer who is able to grasp user needs and solve problems. A strong portfolio of successful UX and other technical projects is essential.

What you'll be doing:

• Understand product specifications and user psychology

• Conduct concept and usability testing and gather feedback

• Create personas through user research and data

• Define the right interaction model and evaluate its success

• Develop wireframes and prototypes around customer needs

• Find creative ways to solve UX problems (e.g. usability, findability)

• Work with UI designers to implement attractive designs

• Communicate design ideas and prototypes to developers

• Keep abreast of competitor products and industry trends

Requirements

• Proven experience as a UX Designer within the travel/events/meetings industry

• Solid grasp of user-centered design (UCD), planning and conducting user research, user testing, A/B testing, rapid prototyping, heuristic analysis, usability and accessibility concerns

• Strong portfolio of design projects

• Background in project management and research

• Familiarity with interaction design and information architecture

• Knowledge of HTML/CSS; JavaScript is a plus

• Problem-solving aptitude

• Analytical mind with a business acumen

• Excellent communication skills

• BSc in Design, Computer Science, Engineering or a related field

Benefits

• Work from Anywhere: Break free from the traditional office constraints! With TROOP's work-from-anywhere policy, you can choose your workspace within your time zone.

• Join the Pioneering Team: As part of the initial team at TROOP , you'll be at the forefront of an extraordinary adventure. Picture yourself shaping the future of a fast-growing technology company, where your ideas and contributions truly make a difference.

• Paid Time Off: We provide a generous PTO policy of 23 days per year, allowing you ample opportunity to relax, recharge, and have some well-deserved fun.

• Discover an Incredible, Supportive Team and Diverse Culture: Prepare to be amazed by the exceptional individuals who form TROOP's team. Collaborate with brilliant, multicultural minds, where diverse backgrounds unite for unparalleled collaboration… See here: ( https://youtu.be/14zv5h3Fakg)

• Supported by Top Investors: TROOP's remarkable journey is backed by prestigious investors, such as the Madrona Group , who recognize its immense potential. Join forces with a company that has garnered the trust and support of the best in the industry.

• Possibility to become a shareholder: The ultimate advantage at TROOP. By owning shares, you actively shape the company's future, share in its success, witness astounding growth, and enjoy a long-term investment that aligns your personal triumphs with TROOP's achievements.

• Access to TalkLife: We offer access to “Talk Life” as a 100% free, anonymous platform where employees connect with others at any time for peer-to-peer support, offering and receiving advice, empathy, and encouragement regarding any situation on their mind. It is a complement to professional help and is available 24/7. ( https://www.talklife.com/ )

• Mental Health Budget: 200 USD yearly budget assistance for mental health support for all our employees.

• Unforgettable Adventures: At our company, we cherish the bonds we create and the time we spend together. So, as a special treat, we believe in celebrating our team's hard work and dedication. Each year, we embark on an incredible one-year trip to a surprise location, courtesy of TROOP. You'll have the opportunity to explore new cultures, create lasting memories, and bond with your colleagues in a unique and exciting way.

TROOP hires globally, and we are 100% virtual. We are looking for someone based in South Africa, Spain or anywhere else on CET or CAT to enable interaction with TROOPERS based in Europe, South Africa and the USA.
